statement.en: Hobgoblins are small hairy men, kin of brownies, doing house chores while the family sleeps.

claims.quote: While brownies are more peaceful creatures, hobgoblins are more fond of practical jokes. They also seem to be able to shapeshift, as seen in one of Puck's monologues in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

statement.id: Hobgoblin lebih gemar bercanda daripada brownie dan tampaknya bisa berubah wujud, seperti monolog Puck.
statement.en: Hobgoblins like pranks more than brownies and seem able to shapeshift, as in a monologue by Puck.

claims.quote: Like other fairy folk, hobgoblins are easily annoyed. They can be mischievous, frightening, and even dangerous. Attempts to give them clothing will often banish them forever

statement.id: Hobgoblin mudah tersinggung, bisa jahil, menakutkan, berbahaya; diberi pakaian membuat mereka pergi selamanya.
statement.en: Hobgoblins are easily annoyed and can be dangerous; giving them clothing often banishes them forever.

claims.quote: Dobby is another term for hobgoblin in Lancashire and Yorkshire according to the folklorist Elizabeth Mary Wright, especially one that is a relentless prankster.

statement.id: Menurut Elizabeth Mary Wright, dobby sebutan lain hobgoblin di Lancashire dan Yorkshire.
statement.en: According to Elizabeth Mary Wright, dobby is another term for hobgoblin in Lancashire and Yorkshire.

claims.quote: Le hobgoblin est une créature légendaire du folklore britannique. Il est décrit comme amical et parfois serviable, vivant dans les habitations des campagnes. Dans le folklore anglais plus tardif, il est parfois décrit comme un esprit diabolique et confondu avec le gobelin.

statement.id: Hobgoblin makhluk legenda Britania (britannique), ramah, tinggal di rumah pedesaan; kemudian kadang dianggap roh jahat dan dicampur dengan goblin (gobelin).
statement.en: The hobgoblin is a legendary British (britannique) creature, friendly, living in country homes; later sometimes an evil spirit confused with the goblin (gobelin).

claims.quote: Une hypothèse dérive hobgoblin du gallois hob, « sautiller », et coblyn « gobelin » ; ce « gobelin sautillant » pouvant être rattaché au personnage légendaire de Puck. Ou bien Hob dérive de l'anglais hob, « foyer »

statement.id: Hob mungkin dari kata Wales (gallois) hob melompat, atau kata Inggris (anglais) hob perapian.
statement.en: Hob may come from Welsh (gallois) hob to hop, or English (anglais) hob hearth.

claims.quote: De même Hob est le diminutif de Robert/Robin, rattachant peut-être le hobgoblin au Robin Goodfellow (Puck).

statement.id: Hob nama kecil Robert/Robin, mungkin mengaitkan hobgoblin dengan Robin Goodfellow (Puck).
statement.en: Hob is a diminutive of Robert/Robin, perhaps linking the hobgoblin to Robin Goodfellow (Puck).

short_description.id: Aufhocker atau Huckup adalah makhluk pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang melompat ke punggung pejalan malam dan makin berat di setiap langkah.
short_description.en: The Aufhocker or Huckup is a shapeshifter of German folklore that leaps onto the backs of night travellers and grows heavier with every step.

long_description.id: Aufhocker (bahasa Jerman Hilir Huckup) adalah makhluk pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang tak punya bentuk tetap: ia bisa tampil sebagai goblin, perempuan cantik, orang mati, atau berbagai hewan seperti beruang, anak sapi, manusia serigala, atau anjing. Namanya berarti "yang melompat ke atas", sebab ia melompat ke punggung korbannya, sering pencuri dan penjahat yang perlu diberi pelajaran, pejalan sendirian, atau perempuan tua.
long_description.en: The Aufhocker (Low German Huckup) is a shapeshifter of German folklore with no fixed form: goblin, lovely woman, corpse, or a beast such as a bear, calf, werewolf or dog are all among its guises. Its name means 'leap upon', because it springs onto its victims' backs, often thieves and wrongdoers who need a lesson, lone travellers or old women.

long_description.id: Sebagai roh penekan, ia duduk di bahu pejalan malam dan makin berat di setiap langkah, sehingga korbannya lumpuh, sesak, dan tak bisa menoleh; banyak yang mati kelelahan karena ia tak bisa dienyahkan. Korban dapat bebas bila berhasil sampai di rumah, atau bila datang cahaya fajar, doa, atau dentang lonceng. Serangan ini terjadi di tempat tertentu: jembatan, persimpangan, mata air, hutan, jalan cekung, dan pemakaman.
long_description.en: As a pressure spirit it sits on a night walker's shoulders and grows heavier at each step, leaving the victim paralysed, oppressed and unable to turn around; many die of exhaustion because it cannot be shaken off. A victim can be freed by reaching home, or by dawn light, a prayer or the ringing of bells. Such attacks happen at particular places: bridges, crossroads, springs, woods, sunken lanes and cemeteries.

long_description.id: Kepercayaan akan Aufhocker berakar pada ketakutan terhadap mayat hidup (Wiedergänger): laporan tertua berbicara tentang "mayat yang melompat ke punggung", bukan kobold atau hantu. Sebagian versi menyebut ia merobek leher korban, yang dikaitkan dengan vampirisme. Mitos serupa ada di banyak bagian Eropa, seperti Ganipote di Charente-Maritime, Prancis.
long_description.en: Belief in the Aufhocker is rooted in fear of the revenant (Wiedergänger): the oldest reports speak of 'corpses that leap onto one's back', not of kobolds or ghosts. Some versions say it tears out its victims' throats, which links it with vampirism. Similar myths exist across much of Europe, such as the Ganipote of Charente-Maritime in France.

who.en: A spirit that leaps on your back.

famous_for.id: Diusir cahaya fajar, doa, atau lonceng.
famous_for.en: Banished by dawn, prayer or bells.

did_you_know.id: Aufhocker dari Düren yang disebut Hackestüpp mula-mula menemani korbannya sebagai anak anjing yang lucu sebelum melompat ke punggungnya.
did_you_know.en: The Hackestüpp of Düren, an Aufhocker, first follows its victims as a playful little dog before leaping onto their backs.

claims.quote: The aufhocker ( German: [ˈaʊfˌhɔkɐ] ) or huckup ( German: [ˈhʊkˌʔʊp] ) is a shapeshifter in German folklore.

statement.id: Aufhocker atau huckup adalah makhluk pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Jerman (German).
statement.en: The aufhocker or huckup is a shapeshifter of German folklore.

claims.quote: The Aufhocker is described in German legend as having an unidentifiable shape because it takes on shapes such as a goblin, a beautiful woman, a dead man, or various animals.

statement.id: Aufhocker digambarkan tak punya bentuk yang dapat dikenali karena mengambil rupa goblin, perempuan cantik, orang mati, atau berbagai hewan.
statement.en: The Aufhocker is said to have no identifiable shape, taking forms such as a goblin, a beautiful woman, a dead man or various animals.

claims.quote: The name Aufhocker means "leap upon". This name is used because according to legend, the Aufhocker would leap upon the back of its victims which are often thieves and criminals that need to be taught a lesson. Other common targets in the Aufhocker legend are lone travelers and old women.

statement.id: Nama Aufhocker berarti "melompat ke atas", karena menurut legenda ia melompat ke punggung korbannya, sering pencuri dan penjahat yang perlu diberi pelajaran, juga pejalan sendirian dan perempuan tua.
statement.en: The name Aufhocker means 'leap upon', since legend says it leaps onto victims' backs, often thieves and criminals needing a lesson, also lone travellers and old women.

claims.quote: The victims often die of exhaustion because the Aufhocker cannot be shaken off or killed. However, it is believed that travelers can free themselves if they are able to make it home before being killed. These attacks often occur in specific locations such as bridges, crossroads, springs, woods, on a path through a hollow, and cemeteries.

statement.id: Korban sering mati kelelahan karena Aufhocker tak bisa dienyahkan atau dibunuh, tetapi pejalan bisa bebas bila sempat sampai di rumah; serangan terjadi di jembatan, persimpangan, mata air, hutan, jalan cekung, dan pemakaman.
statement.en: Victims often die of exhaustion as the Aufhocker cannot be shaken off or killed, but travellers can free themselves by reaching home; attacks occur at bridges, crossroads, springs, woods, hollow paths and cemeteries.

claims.quote: Similar myths can be found in most of Europe. In the Charente-Maritime département of France, the Ganipote is depicted as having similar traits.

statement.id: Mitos serupa ditemukan di sebagian besar Eropa (Europe); di Charente-Maritime, Prancis (France), Ganipote digambarkan bersifat serupa.
statement.en: Similar myths are found across most of Europe; in Charente-Maritime, France, the Ganipote is described with similar traits.

claims.quote: Der Aufhocker (niederdeutsch Huckup, sorbisch Bubak) ist in der Mythologie ein koboldartiger Druckgeist, der Wanderern, die nachts noch unterwegs sind, auf die Schultern oder den Rücken springt und mit jedem Schritt schwerer wird. ... Der Aufhocker bleibt auf dem Wanderer sitzen, bis dieser durch das heraufbrechende Licht, ein Gebet oder Glockenläuten von ihm erlöst wird

statement.id: Aufhocker (Jerman Hilir Huckup, Sorbia Bubak) adalah roh penekan mirip kobold yang melompat ke bahu atau punggung pejalan malam dan makin berat di setiap langkah; ia tetap duduk di sana sampai pejalan dibebaskan oleh cahaya fajar, doa, atau dentang lonceng.
statement.en: The Aufhocker (Low German Huckup, Sorbian Bubak) is a kobold-like pressure spirit that leaps onto the shoulders or back of night travellers and grows heavier each step; it stays there until the traveller is freed by dawn light, a prayer or bells.

claims.quote: Manchmal treten die Aufhocker zunächst als mitleiderregende alte Frauen in Erscheinung; sie können aber auch Tiergestalten wie Bär, Kalb (wie beim Bahkauv), Werwolf (wie beim Stüpp) oder Hund (wie beim Sürthgens Mossel) annehmen.

statement.id: Aufhocker kadang muncul sebagai perempuan tua yang memancing iba, tetapi juga bisa berwujud hewan seperti beruang, anak sapi (Bahkauv), manusia serigala (Stüpp), atau anjing.
statement.en: Aufhockers sometimes first appear as pitiable old women, but can also take animal forms such as a bear, calf (Bahkauv), werewolf (Stüpp) or dog.

claims.quote: Typische Spukorte wie Bäche, Brücken, Seen, Wälder, Gräben, Wegkreuzungen, Hohlwege, Kirchhöfe und Mord- oder Richtstätten sind die übliche Stelle für eine Begegnung mit dem Aufhocker

statement.id: Tempat angker yang khas seperti sungai kecil, jembatan, danau, hutan, parit, persimpangan, jalan cekung, pemakaman, serta tempat pembunuhan atau eksekusi adalah lokasi umum pertemuan dengan Aufhocker.
statement.en: Typical haunted places such as brooks, bridges, lakes, woods, ditches, crossroads, sunken lanes, churchyards and murder or execution sites are where one usually meets the Aufhocker.

claims.quote: Seine Ursprünge hat der Glaube an den Aufhocker jedoch in der Furcht vor dem Wiedergänger, dem Untoten. Die ältesten Berichte über Aufhocker sprechen eindeutig von „aufhuckenden Leichen“ und nicht von Kobolden oder Gespenstern.

statement.id: Kepercayaan akan Aufhocker berakar pada ketakutan terhadap Wiedergänger (mayat hidup); laporan tertua jelas berbicara tentang "mayat yang melompat ke punggung" (aufhuckenden Leichen), bukan kobold atau hantu.
statement.en: Belief in the Aufhocker stems from fear of the Wiedergänger (revenant); the oldest reports clearly speak of 'corpses leaping onto backs' (aufhuckenden Leichen), not kobolds or ghosts.

claims.quote: The Aufhocker is a very dangerous theriomorph that is sometimes said to tear out the throats of humans instead of killing its victims from exhaustion. The version of the Aufhocker that attacks victims' throats is linked to vampirism.

statement.id: Aufhocker kadang dikatakan merobek leher manusia alih-alih membunuh korban dengan kelelahan; versi ini dikaitkan dengan vampirisme.
statement.en: The Aufhocker is sometimes said to tear out human throats rather than exhaust its victims; this version is linked to vampirism.

claims.quote: Um solch einen Aufhocker handelt es sich auch bei dem Hackestüpp von Düren, der seine Opfer zunächst als verspieltes Hündchen begleitet, ihnen dann auf den Rücken springt, sich nicht mehr abschütteln lässt und von Schritt zu Schritt schwerer wird.

statement.id: Hackestüpp dari Düren juga Aufhocker: mula-mula menemani korbannya sebagai anak anjing yang lucu, lalu melompat ke punggung mereka, tak bisa dienyahkan, dan makin berat di setiap langkah.
statement.en: The Hackestüpp of Düren is such an Aufhocker: it first follows victims as a playful puppy, then leaps onto their backs, cannot be shaken off and grows heavier step by step.

claims.quote: Das Bahkauv („Bachkalb“) ist eine Aachener Sagengestalt, die nachts betrunkene Männer erschrecken und sie auffordern soll, sie auf ihren Schultern zu tragen.

statement.id: Bahkauv ("anak sapi sungai") adalah tokoh legenda Aachen (Aachener) yang konon menakuti lelaki mabuk pada malam hari dan meminta digendong di bahu mereka.
statement.en: The Bahkauv ('brook calf') is an Aachen legend figure said to frighten drunken men at night and demand to be carried on their shoulders.

claims.quote: Der Wanderer ist wie gelähmt, leidet unter Beklemmung und ist unfähig sich umzuwenden.

short_description.id: Puck, juga disebut Goodfellows atau Robin Goodfellow, adalah demon atau peri dalam cerita rakyat Inggris, berupa roh rumah tangga atau roh alam.
short_description.en: Puck, also called the Goodfellows or Robin Goodfellow, is a demon or fairy of English folklore, a household or nature sprite.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore), Puck, juga dikenal sebagai Goodfellows, adalah demon atau peri yang dapat berupa roh rumah tangga maupun roh alam. Asal-usul katanya tidak pasti: kata Inggris ini sudah tercatat dalam bahasa Inggris Kuno (Old English) sebagai puca, dan kata serupa muncul dalam bahasa Norse Kuno (Old Norse) púki serta bahasa Kelt seperti pwca (Wales), bucca (Cornwall), dan púca (Irlandia). Oxford English Dictionary condong ke asal Skandinavia, sedangkan Erin Sebo dari Flinders University berpendapat kata itu berasal dari Irlandia.
long_description.en: In English folklore the Puck, also known as the Goodfellows, is a demon or fairy that may be a household sprite or a nature sprite. The word's origin is unclear: it is already found in Old English as puca, and similar words appear in Old Norse púki and in Celtic tongues as pwca (Welsh), bucca (Cornish) and púca (Irish). The Oxford English Dictionary leaned to a Scandinavian source, while Erin Sebo of Flinders University argues it came from Irish.

long_description.id: Puck juga dapat disebut Goodfellows atau Hobgoblin, dengan Hob sebagai ganti Rob atau Robin, merujuk pada tokoh Robin Goodfellow. Seperti sebutan "the good folk" untuk peri, nama itu mencerminkan upaya menyenangkan para peri, yang suka pujian meski jahil. Rujukan tertua "Robin Goodfellow" menurut Oxford English Dictionary berasal dari 1531. Menurut artikel de tentang Puk, makhluk kerdil dalam legenda Nordik (nordischen Volkssagen) yang tinggal bersama manusia; bila diberi makan dan minum teratur ia membawa kemakmuran, tetapi bila diperlakukan buruk ia mendatangkan kerugian besar; artikel itu juga mengaitkannya dengan púca dari Kelt.
long_description.en: Puck may also be called the Goodfellows or Hobgoblin, Hob standing in for Rob or Robin, after the figure Robin Goodfellow. Like calling fairies 'the good folk', the name aimed to please beings fond of flattery despite their mischief. The oldest 'Robin Goodfellow' reference cited by the Oxford English Dictionary dates from 1531. The de article describes the Puk as a dwarfish figure of Nordic legend (nordischen Volkssagen) living alongside people; fed and given drink regularly it brings prosperity, but mistreated it causes grave harm; that article also links it with the Celtic púca.

did_you_know.id: Nama Robin Goodfellow bagi Puck dimaksudkan untuk menyenangkan para peri yang gemar pujian, serupa sebutan "the good folk".
did_you_know.en: The name Robin Goodfellow for Puck was meant to please fairies who loved flattery, much like calling them 'the good folk'.

note.en: Related word and figure in Celtic tongues.

claims.quote: In English folklore, The Puck (/ˈpʌk/), also known as Goodfellows, are demons or fairies which can be domestic sprites or nature sprites.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore), Puck (Goodfellows) demon atau peri, roh rumah atau roh alam; di Britania Raya.
statement.en: In English folklore, the Puck (Goodfellows) are demons or fairies, domestic or nature sprites.

claims.quote: The present-day English word is attested already in Old English as puca (with a diminutive form pucel ). Similar words are attested later in Old Norse (púki , with related forms including Old Swedish puke , Icelandic púki , and Frisian puk ) but also in the Celtic languages (Welsh pwca , Cornish bucca and Irish púca ).

statement.id: Kata ini sudah ada dalam Inggris Kuno (Old English) puca; serupa Norse Kuno (Old Norse) púki, Kelt (Celtic): Wales (Welsh) pwca, Cornwall (Cornish) bucca, Irlandia (Irish) púca; Oxford English Dictionary condong Skandinavia, Erin Sebo dari Flinders University ke Irlandia. (Scandinavian)
statement.en: Attested in Old English as puca; similar to Old Norse púki and Celtic Welsh pwca, Cornish bucca, Irish púca. (Scandinavian)

claims.quote: Puck may also be called The Goodfellows or Hobgoblin, in which Hob may substitute for Rob or Robin. This goes back to the character "Robin Goodfellow" and his name.

statement.id: Puck juga disebut Goodfellows atau Hobgoblin, Hob pengganti Rob atau Robin, dari Robin Goodfellow; seperti the good folk, untuk menyenangkan peri.
statement.en: Puck is also called the Goodfellows or Hobgoblin, Hob for Rob or Robin, from Robin Goodfellow.

claims.quote: The earliest reference to "Robin Goodfellow" cited by the Oxford English Dictionary is from 1531.

statement.id: Rujukan tertua Robin Goodfellow menurut Oxford English Dictionary dari 1531.

claims.quote: ist eine zwergenwüchsige Figur unbestimmten Geschlechts der nordischen Volkssagen. Puks leben mit den Menschen zusammen und gehören in die Gruppe der Elfen aus der germanischen Mythologie.

statement.id: Puk sosok kerdil (zwergenwüchsige) dari legenda Nordik (nordischen Volkssagen), tinggal bersama manusia, golongan elf (Elfen) mitologi Jermanik (germanischen). Dikaitkan dengan púca Kelt (keltischen Púca).
statement.en: The Puk is a dwarfish (zwergenwüchsige) figure of Nordic legend (nordischen Volkssagen), living with people, among the elves (Elfen) of Germanic myth. Linked with the Celtic púca (keltischen Púca).

claims.quote: Wird der Puk mit regelmäßigen Speisen und Getränken gut behandelt, so ist er, im Verbund mit anderen Sagengestalten wie Zwergen und Riesen, in der Lage, das Wohlergehen der Bewohner und deren Tiere positiv bis hin zum Reichtum zu beeinflussen.

statement.en: A Puk given regular food and drink can bring prosperity; it is also linked with the Celtic púca.

claims.quote: Wird er jedoch schlecht behandelt, fügt er den Bewohnern schwere Schäden zu, die nicht selten in Wahnsinn oder mit dem Tod enden.

statement.id: Bila diperlakukan buruk, Puk mendatangkan kerugian besar, bahkan kegilaan atau kematian.
statement.en: Mistreated, the Puk causes grave harm, even madness or death.

short_description.id: Landvættir adalah roh tanah dalam agama Nordik Kuno, kepercayaan rakyat kemudian, dan Heathenry modern, yang terikat pada tempat tertentu dan menentukan kesuburan tanahnya.
short_description.en: Landvættir are land spirits of Old Nordic religion, later folk belief and modern Heathenry, bound to particular places and needed for the land to be fruitful.

long_description.id: Landvættir, "roh tanah", dikenal dalam agama Nordik Kuno, kepercayaan rakyat sesudahnya, dan Heathenry modern. Mereka terikat erat pada tempat tertentu, dan kesejahteraan mereka dianggap syarat agar tanah yang mereka huni subur. Dalam sumber Nordik Kuno mereka bisa berbahaya, sanggup mengusir orang yang tak diinginkan, tetapi juga dapat ditakut-takuti, misalnya dengan hiasan kepala kapal atau níðstöng.
long_description.en: Landvættir, 'land spirits', figure in Old Nordic religion, in the folk belief that followed it and in present-day Heathenry. Each is bound to a particular place, and the fruitfulness of that land was thought to depend on their wellbeing. Old Norse sources show them as potentially dangerous, able to drive away unwanted people, yet capable of being frightened by things like carved ship figureheads or a níðstöng.

long_description.id: Hukum kafir lama Islandia melarang kapal mendekati daratan dengan kepala berukir yang menganga agar roh tanah tidak takut. Landnámabók menceritakan tak seorang pun berani tinggal di tempat Hjörleif menetap karena landvættir, dan para perempuan membawa makanan ke tumpukan batu agar landvættir membuat mereka makmur. Hukum Gulating Norwegia abad ke-13 melarang kepercayaan bahwa gundukan kubur, hutan, dan air terjun dihuni landvættir sebagai bidah.
long_description.en: The old heathen law of Iceland forbade ships to approach land with gaping carved heads lest the land spirits be scared. Landnámabók says that fear of the landvættir kept anyone from living on Hjörleif's former land, and women took food to stone piles hoping the landvættir would make them prosperous. Norway's 13th-century Gulating laws banned the belief that howes, woods and waterfalls were inhabited by landvættir as heresy.

long_description.id: Dalam sebuah kisah saga, seorang penyihir utusan Raja Harald berwujud paus melihat semua gunung dan bukit Islandia penuh roh penjaga, lalu diusir di tiap sisi pulau oleh naga, burung besar, banteng, dan raksasa gunung (bergrisi). Keempat sosok ini kini dipandang sebagai pelindung empat wilayah Islandia dan tampil pada lambang negara serta koin króna.
long_description.en: In a saga account a warlock sent by King Harald in the shape of a whale saw all the mountains and hills of Iceland full of guardian spirits, and was driven off on each side of the island by a dragon, a great bird, a bull and a mountain giant (bergrisi). These four figures are now regarded as protectors of Iceland's four quarters and appear on the coat of arms and the króna coins.

long_description.id: Sebagian sarjana menganggap landvættir roh chthonic atau arwah orang mati, sedangkan yang lain memandangnya roh alam karena kadang mereka menghuni tanah yang tak pernah didiami manusia. Mereka juga dikaitkan dengan elf, kurcaci, dan landdísir.
long_description.en: Some scholars consider landvættir chthonic spirits of the dead, while others see them as nature spirits because they sometimes live in land never settled by people. They have also been linked with elves, dwarfs and landdísir.

literal_meaning.en: guardian spirits of a country; land spirits

origin.en: Old Nordic religion and later folk belief.

did_you_know.en: Iceland's old heathen law required carved figureheads to be removed before land came into sight, so the land spirits would not be frightened.

claims.quote: Landvættir ("land spirits" or "land wights") are spirits of the land in Old Nordic religion, later folk belief and modern Heathenry. They are closely associated with specific locations and their wellbeing is presented as being required for the land they inhabit to be fruitful. In Old Norse sources, they are depicted as being potentially harmful and capable of driving away unwanted individuals

statement.id: Landvættir ("roh tanah") adalah roh tanah dalam agama Nordik Kuno, kepercayaan rakyat sesudahnya, dan Heathenry modern; mereka terikat pada tempat tertentu, kesejahteraannya syarat kesuburan tanah, dan dalam sumber Nordik Kuno mereka bisa berbahaya serta mampu mengusir orang yang tak diinginkan.
statement.en: Landvættir ('land spirits') are spirits of the land in Old Nordic religion, later folk belief and modern Heathenry; tied to specific places, their wellbeing is needed for the land to be fruitful, and Old Norse sources show them as potentially harmful and able to drive away unwanted people.

claims.quote: Translation: It was the beginning of the preamble of the heathen laws that men should not take ships to sea with carved figure heads upon their sterns, but if they did, they should take them off before they came in sight of land

statement.id: Pembukaan hukum kafir menyatakan orang tidak boleh berlayar dengan kepala berukir di kapalnya, dan bila ada, harus melepasnya sebelum daratan terlihat.
statement.en: The preamble of the heathen laws said men should not sail with carved figureheads, and if they did, should remove them before land came in sight.

claims.quote: Later, the book states that no one dared live where Hjörleif had settled because of the landvættir.

statement.id: Landnámabók kemudian menyatakan tak seorang pun berani tinggal di tempat Hjörleif menetap karena landvættir.
statement.en: The book later states no one dared live where Hjörleif had settled because of the landvættir.

claims.quote: In this account, the women take food to stone piles or flat stones, hoping that in return the landvættir would make them prosperous.

statement.id: Dalam catatan itu, para perempuan membawa makanan ke tumpukan batu atau batu datar dengan harapan landvættir membuat mereka makmur.
statement.en: In this account, women take food to stone piles or flat stones hoping the landvættir will make them prosperous.

claims.quote: The Norwegian Gulating laws, written in the latter half of the 13th century, made illegal the belief that howes, wooded areas and waterfalls, were inhabited by landvættir, considering it a heresy and belonging to the heathen religion.

statement.id: Hukum Gulating Norwegia dari paruh kedua abad ke-13 melarang kepercayaan bahwa gundukan kubur, hutan, dan air terjun dihuni landvættir, karena dianggap bidah dan bagian agama kafir.
statement.en: Norway's Gulating laws of the later 13th century outlawed the belief that howes, woods and waterfalls were inhabited by landvættir, deeming it heresy and heathen.

claims.quote: King Harald told a warlock to hie to Iceland in some altered shape, and to try what he could learn there to tell him: and he set out in the shape of a whale. ... where he saw all the mountains and hills full of guardian-spirits, some great, some small.

statement.id: Raja Harald menyuruh seorang penyihir pergi ke Islandia dalam wujud lain; ia berangkat sebagai paus dan melihat semua gunung dan bukit penuh roh penjaga, besar dan kecil.
statement.en: King Harald sent a warlock to Iceland in altered shape; he went as a whale and saw all the mountains and hills full of guardian spirits, great and small.

claims.quote: First on the East side by a large dragon followed by snakes, toads and lizards who blew atter, or poison, at him, then on the North side by a great bird with many smaller birds, next in the West a large bull followed by beasts and other landvættir, and finally a huge bergrisi with an iron staff in the South

statement.id: Ia diusir di sisi timur oleh naga besar yang diikuti ular, kodok, dan kadal penyembur racun, di utara oleh burung besar, di barat oleh banteng besar beserta landvættir lain, dan di selatan oleh bergrisi raksasa bertongkat besi.
statement.en: He was driven off in the east by a great dragon with poison-blowing snakes, toads and lizards, in the north by a great bird, in the west by a great bull with other landvættir, and in the south by a huge bergrisi with an iron staff.

claims.quote: Les quatre Landvættir sont aujourd'hui considérés comme les protecteurs des quatre quartiers d'Islande : le dragon (Dreki) dans le Nord-Est, l'aigle ou griffon (Gammur) dans de Nord-Ouest, le taureau (Griðungur) dans le Sud-Ouest, et le géant (Bergrisi) dans le Sud-Est. Les quatre Landvættir de l'Islande sont représentés sur les Armoiries de l'Islande et sur l'envers des pièces

statement.id: Empat landvættir kini dianggap pelindung empat wilayah Islandia: naga (Dreki), elang atau griffin (Gammur), banteng (Griðungur), dan raksasa (Bergrisi); keempatnya tampil pada lambang Islandia dan sisi belakang koin króna.
statement.en: The four landvættir are now regarded as protectors of Iceland's four quarters: the dragon (Dreki), eagle or griffin (Gammur), bull (Griðungur) and giant (Bergrisi); they appear on the Icelandic arms and the reverse of króna coins.

claims.quote: Some scholars have suggested that landvættir are chthonic and spirits of the dead, but others have interpreted them as nature spirits, since they sometimes live in land that has never been populated.

statement.id: Sebagian sarjana menduga landvættir adalah roh chthonic dan arwah orang mati, sedangkan yang lain menafsirkannya sebagai roh alam karena kadang menghuni tanah yang tak pernah didiami.
statement.en: Some scholars suggest landvættir are chthonic spirits of the dead, while others interpret them as nature spirits because they sometimes live in never-populated land.

claims.quote: Landvættir have been variously connected by scholars to other beings believed to inhabit the land such as elves, dwarfs and landdísir, with which they were potentially identified at different points in history.

statement.id: Para sarjana mengaitkan landvættir dengan makhluk lain penghuni tanah seperti elf, kurcaci, dan landdísir, yang mungkin pernah disamakan dengannya pada masa berbeda.
statement.en: Scholars have linked landvættir to other land-dwelling beings such as elves, dwarfs and landdísir, with which they may have been identified at different times.

claims.quote: As a compound, land-vættir has been variously translated as "guardian spirits of a country", "land-spirits", "landwights" or "nature spirits".

statement.id: Sebagai kata majemuk, land-vættir diterjemahkan antara lain sebagai "roh penjaga negeri", "roh tanah", atau "roh alam".
statement.en: As a compound, land-vættir has been rendered 'guardian spirits of a country', 'land-spirits', 'landwights' or 'nature spirits'.

short_description.id: Shikigami adalah roh pendamping dalam tradisi Onmyōdō yang kisah-kisahnya menampilkan beragam rupa dan tugas.
short_description.en: Shikigami are familiar spirits in Onmyōdō whose stories give them varied forms and tasks.

long_description.id: Shikigami disebut sebagai kami atau roh pendamping yang dipanggil dalam tradisi Onmyōdō. Nama lain yang tercatat ialah shikijin dan shiki no kami. Kisah-kisah menggambarkan mereka sebagai anak, lelaki muda, hewan kecil, atau setan; dalam banyak kisah wujudnya justru tidak terlihat. Dalam Konjaku monogatari, praktisi onmyōji menggunakan shikigami untuk sihir, ramalan, serta perintah sehari-hari.
long_description.en: Shikigami are described as kami or familiar spirits invoked in Onmyōdō. Recorded alternative names include shikijin and shiki no kami. Stories portray them as children, young men, small animals, or demons; in many accounts their form remains unseen. Konjaku monogatari says onmyōji practitioners summon them for magic, divination, and everyday commands.

long_description.id: Asal konsepnya diperdebatkan. Sebuah ensiklopedia menghubungkannya dengan dua belas dewa pelindung bulanan pada papan ramalan shikiban dan dengan hewan-hewan yang terkait pembagian waktu. Sebuah kajian menunjukkan bahwa para sarjana juga menafsirkan shikigami sebagai lambang metode ramalan, kutukan, ataupun makhluk gaib. Karena itu, gambaran roh pembantu adalah salah satu cara memahami tokoh ini, bukan definisi tunggal yang diterima semua sumber. Perbedaan penuturan dalam sastra klasik turut menjelaskan mengapa rupanya begitu beragam.
long_description.en: The concept’s origins are debated. An encyclopedia links it to twelve monthly tutelary deities on a shikiban divination board and to animals associated with the hours. A study shows that scholars have interpreted shikigami as a metaphor for divination, a curse, or a supernatural being. The familiar-spirit account is therefore one interpretation, not a settled definition. Variations in classical narratives help explain their many forms.

short_description.id: Myling adalah arwah anak yang dibunuh dan tidak dikuburkan dengan layak dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, yang meminta dibawa ke tanah suci pemakaman.
short_description.en: In Scandinavian folklore a myling is the ghost of a murdered child left unburied, who demands to be carried to consecrated ground.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, mylingar adalah penjelmaan arwah anak-anak yang terpaksa berkeliaran di bumi sampai mereka dapat membujuk seseorang untuk menguburkan mereka dengan layak. Menurut kepercayaan rakyat Swedia, myling adalah mayat hidup bayi yang belum dibaptis, dibunuh dan disembunyikan ibunya; kadang bayi itu bahkan dikubur di bawah lantai kayu pondok untuk menutupi kelahiran yang tak diinginkan.
long_description.en: In Scandinavian folklore mylingar are the ghostly forms of children's souls forced to wander the earth until they can persuade someone to bury them properly. In Swedish folk belief a myling is the revenant of an unbaptised newborn murdered and hidden by its mother, sometimes even buried under the wooden floor of the cottage to conceal the unwanted birth.

long_description.id: Myling, yang dikenal juga sebagai utburd di Norwegia, útburður di Islandia, serta ihtiriekko dan liekkiö di Finlandia, konon mengejar pengembara yang sendirian di malam hari dan melompat ke punggung mereka, meminta dibawa ke pemakaman. Ia makin berat saat mendekati pemakaman sampai pembawanya bisa terbenam ke tanah, dan bila orang itu gagal mencapai pemakaman, myling membunuhnya dengan murka.
long_description.en: The myling, also called utburd in Norwegian, útburður in Icelandic and ihtiriekko or liekkiö in Finnish, reportedly pursues people walking alone after dark, leaps onto their backs and insists on being taken to the graveyard. It grows heavier as the graveyard nears until its bearer may sink into the soil, and if the person fails to reach the cemetery, the myling kills them in rage.

long_description.id: Nyanyiannya di malam hari dapat membongkar kejahatan sang ibu. Myling dapat ditolong dengan memberinya nama, misalnya bila ia berseru "beri aku nama!", atau dengan menemukan jasadnya dan menguburkannya di tanah suci pemakaman.
long_description.en: Its singing at night can reveal the mother's crime. A myling can be helped by giving it a name, for instance when it cries 'give me a name!', or by finding its body and burying it in hallowed ground.

long_description.id: Kata myling berasal dari bahasa Swedia myrding atau mörding, dari bahasa Swedia Kuno myrða, "membunuh", sehingga berarti "yang dibunuh"; kata ini tercatat dalam bahasa Swedia sejak 1647. Keyakinan bahwa myling murka dan menuntut balas membuatnya dianggap salah satu jenis hantu paling mengancam dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia.
long_description.en: The word myling comes from Swedish myrding or mörding, from Old Swedish myrða, 'to murder', and so means 'the murdered one'; it is attested in Swedish since 1647. The belief that mylingar are enraged and vengeful made them one of the most menacing kinds of ghost in Scandinavian folklore.

short_description.id: Banshee adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia yang kemunculan ratapannya menandai ajal anggota keluarga.
short_description.en: A banshee is a female spirit in Irish folklore whose wailing heralds the death of a family member.

long_description.id: Secara etimologi, nama banshee berasal dari bahasa Irlandia Kuno ben síde yang berarti wanita dari gundukan peri [banshee-c01]. Nama ini berhubungan dengan bukit atau gundukan kuno di pedesaan Irlandia [banshee-c02]. Sosok ini digambarkan berambut panjang terurai yang sedang disisir, memakai jubah kelabu di atas gaun hijau dengan mata merah karena menangis [banshee-c03, banshee-c04]. Kesaksian Ann Lady Fanshawe mencatat penampakan berbaju putih dengan rambut merah dan rona wajah pucat [banshee-c05].
long_description.en: Etymologically, the name banshee derives from Old Irish ben síde meaning woman of the fairy mound [banshee-c01]. Her name connects to ancient mounds across the Irish countryside [banshee-c02]. She is depicted with long streaming hair that she combs, wearing a grey cloak over a green dress with red eyes from weeping [banshee-c03, banshee-c04]. A firsthand account by Ann Lady Fanshawe recorded a figure in white with red hair and a ghastly complexion [banshee-c05].

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi lisan, banshee dikenal lewat jeritan atau ratapan yang menandai kematian seseorang [banshee-c01, banshee-c10, banshee-c11]. Legenda ini berakar dari tradisi keening atau ratapan perempuan pelayat dalam upacara pemakaman di Irlandia [banshee-c06, banshee-c07, banshee-c12, banshee-c13]. Perbedaan utamanya adalah banshee meramalkan kematian sebelum peristiwa itu terjadi [banshee-c14, banshee-c15]. Suara ratapan ini kerap disalahartikan sebagai jeritan hewan seperti rubah [banshee-c16]. Sosok ini juga dikisahkan mencuci pakaian bernoda darah di sungai serta membuntuti keluarga tertentu hingga ke negeri lain [banshee-c17, banshee-c18, banshee-c19, banshee-c20, banshee-c21].
long_description.en: In oral tradition, the banshee is known for screams and wails that herald someone's death [banshee-c01, banshee-c10, banshee-c11]. This lore stems from traditional funeral keening laments performed by women in Ireland [banshee-c06, banshee-c07, banshee-c12, banshee-c13]. The vital difference is that banshees predict a passing before it occurs [banshee-c14, banshee-c15]. Her cry is often mistaken for animal calls like a fox [banshee-c16]. Legends also describe her washing bloodstained clothes in rivers and following families across foreign lands [banshee-c17, banshee-c18, banshee-c19, banshee-c20, banshee-c21].

cultural_context.id: Bagi masyarakat Irlandia, mitos banshee mencerminkan tradisi perkabungan komunal melalui ratapan duka para pelayat, sekaligus menjadi pengingat leluhur dan batas takdir kematian bagi keluarga-keluarga tua.
cultural_context.en: In Irish culture, the banshee myth reflects communal mourning customs through funeral keening laments while serving as an ancestral reminder of mortality for traditional families.

learning_questions.en: Why is the banshee regarded in traditional folklore as a harbinger of death rather than an active murderer?

claims.quote: A banshee (/ˈbænʃiː/ BAN-shee; Modern Irish bean sí  [bʲanˠ ˈʃiː] , from Old Irish: ben síde  [bʲen ˈʃiːðʲe] , "woman of the fairy mound" or "fairy woman") is a female spirit in Irish folklore who heralds the death of a family member

statement.id: Banshee adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia yang menandai kematian anggota keluarga.
statement.en: A banshee is a female spirit in Irish folklore who heralds the death of a family member.

claims.quote: Her name is connected to the mythologically important tumuli or "mounds" that dot the Irish countryside, which are known as síde  (singular síd ) in Old Irish.

statement.id: Nama banshee terhubung dengan gundukan kuno di pedesaan Irlandia yang dikenal sebagai side dalam bahasa Irlandia Kuno.
statement.en: Her name connects to ancient mounds across Ireland known as side in Old Irish.

claims.quote: Sometimes she has long streaming hair, which she may be seen combing, with some legends specifying she can only keen while combing her hair.

statement.id: Banshee kadang terlihat memiliki rambut panjang terurai yang sedang disisir.
statement.en: She is sometimes seen with long streaming hair that she combs.

claims.quote: She wears a grey cloak over a green dress, and her eyes are red from continual weeping.

statement.id: Banshee digambarkan mengenakan jubah abu-abu di atas gaun hijau dengan mata merah karena terus menangis.
statement.en: She wears a grey cloak over a green dress with red eyes from weeping.

claims.quote: She may be dressed in white with red hair and a ghastly complexion, according to a firsthand account by Ann, Lady Fanshawe in her Memoirs.

statement.id: Kesaksian Ann Lady Fanshawe mencatat sosok berpakaian putih dengan rambut merah dan rona wajah pucat.
statement.en: An account by Ann Lady Fanshawe describes a figure in white with red hair and ghastly complexion.

claims.quote: In Ireland and parts of Scotland, a traditional part of mourning is the keening woman (bean chaointe ), who wails a lament

statement.id: Di Irlandia dan Skotlandia, bagian tradisi perkabungan mencakup perempuan peratap yang melantunkan duka.
statement.en: In Ireland and Scotland, mourning traditionally includes keening women who wail laments.

claims.quote: This keening woman may in some cases be a professional, and the best keeners would be in high demand.

statement.id: Perempuan peratap kadang kala merupakan tenaga profesional yang sangat diminati.
statement.en: The keening woman was sometimes a professional in high demand.

claims.quote: When several banshees appear at once, it indicates the death of someone great or holy. The tales sometimes recounted that the woman, though called a fairy, was a ghost, often of a specific murdered woman, or a mother who died in childbirth.

statement.id: Kemunculan beberapa banshee sekaligus menandai wafatnya orang suci atau tokoh agung.
statement.en: Multiple banshees appearing together signifies the demise of someone great or holy.

claims.quote: In some parts of Leinster, she is referred to as the bean chaointe  ('keening woman') whose wail can be so piercing that it shatters glass.

statement.id: Di beberapa wilayah Leinster, banshee disebut perempuan peratap yang jeritannya dapat memecahkan kaca.
statement.en: In parts of Leinster, she is called a keening woman whose wail can shatter glass.

claims.quote: The Banshee is a fairy from old Irish folklore. It is said that if you hear a Banshee’s scream, it is a warning that someone close to you is on the verge of passing.

statement.id: Banshee merupakan peri dari cerita rakyat Irlandia yang jeritannya menjadi pertanda ajal seseorang di dekatnya.
statement.en: The banshee is a fairy from Irish folklore whose scream warns of someone's passing.

claims.quote: The Banshee is known for its spine-tingling scream. You will hear many different accounts from across Ireland about the true sound, but the Banshee is said to sound like a woman wailing in a distressed manner.
claims.locator: Section 2. What does a Banshee sound like

statement.id: Banshee dikenal dengan jeritan mengerikan yang terdengar seperti perempuan meratap dalam kesedihan mendalam.
statement.en: The banshee is known for a spine-tingling scream sounding like a wailing woman.

claims.quote: Many believe that the legend of the Banshee originated from the tradition of ‘Keening‘, which is a passionate expression of grief.
claims.locator: Section It originated with Keening, paragraph 1

statement.id: Legenda banshee diyakini berakar dari tradisi meratap atau keening yang merupakan luapan rasa berduka.
statement.en: The legend of the banshee is believed to stem from the grieving tradition of keening.

claims.quote: The word ‘Keen’ comes from the Gaelic word ‘caoineadh’, which means to cry or weep and it used to be an Irish funeral ritual.
claims.locator: Section It originated with Keening, paragraph 2

statement.id: Kata keen berasal dari bahasa Gaelik caoineadh yang berarti menangis atau meratap dalam ritual pemakaman.
statement.en: The word keen comes from Gaelic caoineadh meaning to weep in Irish funeral rituals.

claims.quote: the main difference between Banshees and Keening women is that the Banshees can predict the passing of someone, which is why they spark fear in many.
claims.locator: Section It originated with Keening, paragraph 4

statement.id: Perbedaan pokok banshee dengan pelayat manusia adalah banshee meramalkan kematian sebelum terjadi.
statement.en: The key difference is that banshees predict someone's death beforehand.

claims.quote: It is said that the Banshee’s scream foretells the passing of someone close to the one who hears her scream.

statement.id: Jeritan banshee diyakini menubuatkan meninggalnya seseorang yang dekat dengan pendengar jeritan tersebut.
statement.en: Her scream is said to foretell the passing of someone close to the listener.

claims.quote: While strongly liked to the traditional of ‘Keening’, it is likely that many mistake the Banshee scream with the sound of an animal, like a fox.
claims.locator: Section FAQs about the Banshee, question 1

statement.id: Banyak orang mengira jeritan banshee bersumber dari suara satwa malam seperti rubah.
statement.en: Many people mistake the banshee cry for the sound of an animal like a fox.

claims.quote: came upon a grim and wizened old woman washing armour and fine robes, all stained with blood, in the swift running river.
claims.locator: Section Richard de Clare narrative, paragraph 1

statement.id: Pasukan Richard de Clare menjumpai perempuan tua keriput yang mencuci pakaian dan zirah bernoda darah di sungai.
statement.en: Richard de Clare encountered a wizened old woman washing bloodstained clothes in a swift river.

claims.quote: she was the woman of the waters of misery, who made her home in the misted mounds of the fairies - but she was of the tribes of hell
claims.locator: Section Richard de Clare narrative, paragraph 2

statement.id: Sosok tersebut digambarkan mendiami bukit gundukan peri berkabut.
statement.en: The figure was said to make her home in the misted mounds of the fairies.

claims.quote: The hag was washing human limbs and heads with gory weapons and clothes, till all the waters were defiled with blood, brains, and floating hair.
claims.locator: Section Richard de Clare narrative, paragraph 3

statement.id: Sosok perempuan tua meratap mencuci sisa-sisa bagian tubuh berdarah di aliran air.
statement.en: The hag was seen washing limbs and clothes until waters were defiled with blood.

claims.quote: she has been known to follow families abroad and dog their footsteps in other countries.

statement.id: Banshee dikenal membuntuti garis keturunan keluarga tertentu bahkan hingga ke mancanegara.
statement.en: The banshee has been known to follow families abroad to other countries.

claims.quote: The angry men raised their javelins, but she rose on the wind, yelling more and more words of woe till she vanished.
claims.locator: Section Richard de Clare narrative, paragraph 4

statement.id: Sosok ini dapat membubung tinggi di atas angin sambil berteriak kata-kata duka hingga menghilang.
statement.en: She rose on the wind yelling words of woe until vanishing.

short_description.id: Manannán mac Lir ("anak laut") adalah dewa laut, pejuang, dan raja dunia lain dalam mitologi Gaelik, salah satu Tuatha Dé Danann.
short_description.en: Manannán mac Lir, whose surname means 'son of the Sea', is the Gaelic god of the sea, a warrior and lord of the otherworld, counted among the Tuatha Dé Danann.

long_description.id: Manannán atau Manann, juga Manannán mac Lir ("anak laut"), adalah dewa laut, pejuang, dan raja dunia lain dalam mitologi Gaelik (Gaelic) Irlandia, Man, dan Skotlandia, dan salah satu Tuatha Dé Danann. Ia penguasa dan penjaga dunia lain, yang disebut Emain Ablach ("Pulau Pohon Apel"), Mag Mell ("Dataran Kebahagiaan"), atau Tír Tairngire ("Negeri Perjanjian"). Setelah kedatangan manusia (kaum Milesia), ia menjadi raja atas Tuatha Dé yang tersisa dan memakai kabut gaib (féth fíada) untuk menyembunyikan kediamannya dan sidhe yang lain.
long_description.en: Manannán (or Manann), called Manannán mac Lir, 'son of the Sea', is the sea god, warrior and otherworld king of Irish, Manx and Scottish Gaelic myth, and belongs to the Tuatha Dé Danann. As lord and keeper of the otherworld, his realm goes by several names: Tír Tairngire, the 'Land of Promise'; Mag Mell, the 'Plain of Delights'; and Emain Ablach, the 'Isle of Apple Trees'. After the coming of humans (the Milesians) he became over-king of the remaining Tuatha Dé and uses the mist of invisibility (féth fíada) to hide his home and the other sidhe.

long_description.id: Ia memiliki perahu yang berlayar sendiri, Sguaba Tuinne ("Penyapu Ombak"), kuda Aonbharr yang dapat berlari di atas air dan darat, dan pedang mematikan Fragarach yang menguras kekuatan. Dalam legenda Skotlandia dan Man ia dikenal sebagai Manannan beg mac y Leir, dan Isle of Man (Mannin) umumnya dianggap dinamai menurutnya; ia sekerabat dengan tokoh Wales Manawydan fab Llŷr. Namanya dieja Manandán dalam bahasa Irlandia Kuno dan Mannan dalam bahasa Man. Menurut artikel id, ia dipandang sebagai penjaga dunia lain dan salah satu yang mengantar jiwa ke alam baka, dan juga dikenal sebagai Oirbsiu atau Oirbsen, asal nama Lough Corrib.
long_description.en: He owns a self-sailing boat, Sguaba Tuinne ('Wave-sweeper'), a horse, Aonbharr, that gallops across sea and land alike, and Fragarach, a lethal sword that drains an enemy's strength. In Scottish and Manx legend he is Manannan beg mac y Leir, and the Isle of Man (Mannin) is generally held to be named after him; he is cognate with the Welsh figure Manawydan fab Llŷr. His name is Manandán in Old Irish and Mannan in Manx. According to the id article he is seen as guardian of the otherworld and one who brings souls to the afterlife, and is also known as Oirbsiu or Oirbsen, from whom Lough Corrib takes its name.

famous_for.en: The Isle of Man is named after him.

did_you_know.id: Isle of Man umumnya dianggap dinamai menurut dewa laut Manannán, meski ada yang berpendapat sebaliknya.
did_you_know.en: The Isle of Man is generally thought to be named after the sea god Manannán, though some say the reverse.

short_description.id: Lange Wapper adalah raksasa dan penipu dalam cerita rakyat Flandria, terutama di Antwerpen, yang bisa membesarkan atau mengecilkan diri dan suka mengganggu pemabuk.
short_description.en: Lange Wapper is a giant and trickster of Flemish folklore, above all in Antwerp, who can make himself big or small and likes to torment drunkards.

long_description.id: Lange Wapper adalah tokoh cerita rakyat Flandria, raksasa legendaris sekaligus penipu yang kisahnya terutama diceritakan di kota Antwerpen dan sekitarnya, meski kisah serupa juga ada di kota-kota Flandria lain. Menurut satu versi asal-usulnya, seorang petani menemukannya sebagai bayi dalam kubis merah raksasa di petak peterseli; anak itu diasuh keluarga di Antwerpen dan tumbuh menjadi pemuda kuat yang suka menolong.
long_description.en: Lange Wapper is a figure of Flemish folklore, a legendary giant and trickster whose tales were told especially in Antwerp and nearby towns, though similar stories exist in other Flemish cities. In one account of his origin a farmer found him as a baby inside a giant red cabbage in a parsley bed; the child was raised by an Antwerp family and grew into a strong youth who helped those in need.

long_description.id: Suatu hari ia menyelamatkan seorang nenek dari tenggelam di Sungai Schelde, dan nenek itu memberinya kemampuan membesarkan atau mengecilkan diri; karena lebih suka tampil tinggi, ia dijuluki Lange Wapper. Ia menyamar sebagai anak untuk mendapat air susu, mengganggu pemabuk, dan mencurangi anak-anak dalam permainan, dan tawanya yang mengembik membuat orang menyebutnya "setan air".
long_description.en: After he rescued an old woman who was drowning in the Scheldt, she granted him the power to grow huge or shrink; since he liked best to appear tall, he became known as Lange Wapper. He disguised himself as a child to get breast milk, vexed drunkards and cheated children at games, and his bleating laugh led people to call him 'water devil'.

long_description.id: Dalam satu kisah, seorang lelaki mabuk pulang dari penginapan di Antwerpen dan dikejar sosok misterius; setelah ia bersembunyi di ranjang, Lange Wapper setinggi rumah mengetuk jendelanya dan mengancam akan mematahkan lehernya bila ia mabuk lagi. Satu versi menyebut ia takut pada patung Perawan Maria, yang konon menjelaskan banyaknya patung itu di kota.
long_description.en: In one tale a drunk man walking home from an Antwerp inn is followed by a mysterious figure; after he hides in bed, Lange Wapper, as tall as a house, knocks at his window and threatens to break his neck if he gets drunk again. One version says he feared statues of the Virgin, which supposedly explains how many there are in the city.

did_you_know.id: Proyek jembatan raksasa di Antwerpen dinamai Lange Wapperbrug menurut tokoh ini, tetapi ditolak warga dalam konsultasi publik pada 19 Oktober 2009.
did_you_know.en: A huge bridge project in Antwerp was named Lange Wapperbrug after him, but residents rejected it in a public consultation on 19 October 2009.

short_description.id: Swan Maiden adalah tokoh perempuan gaib dalam pola cerita lintas budaya tentang jubah bulu yang memungkinkan ia pergi dari dunia manusia.
short_description.en: The Swan Maiden is a supernatural woman in cross-cultural stories about a feather robe that lets her leave the human world.

long_description.id: Swan Maiden adalah sebutan bagi pola cerita, bukan satu tokoh dengan riwayat tetap. Kajian folklor menyebut kisah ini tersebar di banyak budaya: seorang perempuan gaib dipaksa menikah dengan lelaki yang menahan benda kunci kebebasannya, lalu pergi ketika benda itu kembali. Dalam salah satu cerita yang dikumpulkan, tujuh perempuan berbaju bulu turun ke danau. Seorang pemburu mengambil jubah si bungsu, menyembunyikannya, dan membuatnya menikah. Ketika anak mereka menemukan jubah itu, perempuan tersebut mengenakannya dan terbang pergi.
long_description.en: Swan Maiden names a story pattern rather than one person with a fixed biography. A folklore study describes stories in many cultures in which a supernatural woman is forced to marry a man who holds the key to her freedom; she leaves when she regains it. In one collected tale, seven feather-robed women descend to a lake. A hunter hides the youngest woman’s robe and makes her marry him. When their child finds it, she puts it on and flies away.

long_description.id: Sebuah versi dari Jepang yang diterjemahkan dalam kumpulan cerita yang sama memakai perempuan kahyangan dan jubah bulu, tanpa menyebut ia berubah menjadi angsa. Seorang nelayan menemukan jubah itu; sang perempuan mengatakan ia tidak dapat kembali ke langit tanpanya. Nelayan akhirnya mengembalikan jubah setelah ia berjanji menari. Ia pun mengenakannya, menari di udara, lalu menghilang. Perbedaan itu menunjukkan bahwa bentuk burung dan akhir cerita bervariasi; unsur yang berulang adalah jubah yang menahan atau membebaskan perempuan gaib.
long_description.en: A Japanese version translated in the same collection features a heavenly maiden and a feather robe without saying she becomes a swan. A fisherman finds the robe; the maiden says she cannot return to heaven without it. He eventually gives it back in return for a dance. She puts it on, dances in the air, and disappears. Bird form and endings vary; the recurring element here is the robe that constrains or releases a supernatural woman.

short_description.id: Amaterasu adalah dewi matahari utama dalam Shinto, penguasa Takama no Hara, dan leluhur ilahi keluarga kekaisaran Japan.
short_description.en: Amaterasu is the chief sun goddess of Shinto, ruler of Takama no Hara, and divine ancestor of Japan's imperial family.

long_description.id: Amaterasu Omikami berarti 'dewa agung yang menerangi langit'. Kisah kelahirannya menempatkannya muncul dari mata kiri Izanagi, dan ia adalah kakak Susanoo sang dewa badai. Ia memerintah dataran langit Takama no Hara.
long_description.en: Amaterasu Omikami means 'great divinity illuminating heaven'. In one birth story she emerges from Izanagi's left eye, and she is the elder sister of the storm god Susanoo. She rules the celestial plain Takama no Hara.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita gua, tindakan Susanoo membuat Amaterasu bersembunyi sehingga dunia gelap. Para dewa menyiapkan cermin dan perhiasan pada pohon sakaki; Uzume menari hingga mereka tertawa. Tajikarao lalu menarik Amaterasu keluar dan terang kembali.
long_description.en: In the cave story, Susanoo's actions cause Amaterasu to hide, leaving the world dark. The gods set a mirror and jewels on a sakaki tree; Uzume dances and they laugh. Tajikarao then pulls Amaterasu out and light returns.

long_description.id: Amaterasu memberi Ninigi tiga benda yang kemudian menjadi lambang kekaisaran Japan. Situs resmi Ise Jingu menyebut Amaterasu sebagai kami leluhur keluarga kekaisaran dan menyatakan cermin suci ditempatkan di Naiku. Lebih dari 1.500 ritual diadakan setiap tahun di kompleks itu.
long_description.en: Amaterasu gives Ninigi three objects that become Japan's imperial regalia. The Ise Jingu shrine describes Amaterasu as the imperial family's ancestral kami and says her sacred mirror is housed at Naiku. More than 1,500 rituals take place at the shrine complex each year.

short_description.id: Ubume adalah roh ibu yang meninggal saat melahirkan dan dalam cerita meminta orang lain menggendong bayinya.
short_description.en: Ubume is the spirit of a mother who died in childbirth and asks others to hold her baby in stories.

long_description.id: Ubume adalah sosok gaib yang paling sering digambarkan sebagai roh perempuan yang meninggal saat melahirkan. Ceritanya memiliki rupa dan identitas yang berbeda-beda. Dalam satu pola kisah, ia tampak seperti perempuan biasa yang menggendong bayi, meminta pejalan kaki memegang anak itu, lalu menghilang. Setelah itu, bayi tersebut ternyata hanya seikat daun atau sebongkah batu. Penjelasan dari kalangan museum juga memasukkan ibu yang meninggalkan anak kecil sebagai bagian dari gambaran ubume.
long_description.en: Ubume is a supernatural figure most often described as the spirit of a woman who died in childbirth. Her identity and appearance vary across stories. In one common pattern she looks like an ordinary woman with a baby, asks a passerby to hold the child, and disappears. The apparent baby turns out to be leaves or a rock. A museum lecture also includes women who left behind young children in its account of ubume.

long_description.id: Ubume dapat disebut yōkai maupun hantu ibu. Kisahnya berkaitan dengan pandangan sosial dan agama tentang persalinan serta kehilangan ibu. Sebuah ringkasan perpustakaan universitas menyebut bahwa pada akhir abad pertengahan, sebagian masyarakat menganggap kematian ibu saat hamil atau melahirkan sebagai dosa dan menyalahkan ibu atas kematian janin. Pengertian itu adalah sikap masa lampau yang dicatat sebagai latar kepercayaan, bukan penilaian atas ibu yang meninggal. Dalam pembahasan seni, kisah hantu, lukisan ukiyo-e, dan kabuki dipandang sebagai media yang mengembangkan tema hantu perempuan.
long_description.en: Ubume may be called both a yōkai and a mother ghost. Her tales are connected with social and religious views about childbirth and maternal loss. A university library summary says that in the late medieval period some people viewed a mother’s death in late pregnancy or childbirth as a sin and blamed her for a fetus’s death. That is a historical attitude reported as context, not a judgment on mothers who died. An art lecture notes that ghost tales, ukiyo-e painting, and kabuki developed ghost themes.

sources.title: Chilling Creatures: The Supernatural in Japanese Art

short_description.id: Rå adalah roh penjaga tempat atau bentang alam tertentu dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia dan Sami, yang bisa membawa untung atau sial bagi manusia.
short_description.en: A rå is a spirit that keeps a particular place or landform in Scandinavian and Sami folklore, able to bring good or bad luck to people.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, rå (jamak rår), kependekan dari rådare ("penguasa"), dari kata råda ("memerintah, menasihati") dan Nordik Kuno ráða, adalah roh penjaga suatu tempat atau bentang alam. Rå dikenal dalam budaya Nordik maupun Sami, tempat ia disebut radie. Manusia perlu menjaga hubungan baik dengannya, karena ia menguasai kekuatan alam dan hewan di bawah asuhannya serta dapat membawa untung atau sial bagi siapa pun yang mengganggu wilayahnya.
long_description.en: In Scandinavian folklore a rå (plural rår), short for rådare ('ruler'), from råda ('to rule, to advise') and Old Norse ráða, is the keeper of a particular place or landform. It is known in Nordic and Sami culture alike, the Sami calling it radie. People had to keep on good terms with it, since it ruled the natural forces and animals in its care and could bring good or bad luck to anyone meddling with its domain.

long_description.id: Rår dibedakan menurut wilayah alam yang dijaganya, seperti skogsrå atau hulder untuk hutan, sjörå untuk air tawar, havsrå untuk air asin, dan bergsrå untuk gunung. Menurut kepercayaan lama, setiap benda, hewan, dan tumbuhan punya rå pelindungnya sendiri, dan rå juga bisa menjaga tempat dan benda milik manusia, seperti skeppsrået (rå kapal) dan gruvrået (rå tambang). Rår dapat tampil berwujud hewan atau manusia; skogsrå dan bergsrå biasanya digambarkan perempuan.
long_description.en: Rår are distinguished by the sphere of nature they keep, such as the skogsrå or hulder of the forest, the sjörå of fresh water, the havsrå of salt water and the bergsrå of mountains. In old belief every object, animal and plant had its own protecting rå, and a rå might also oversee human places and things, such as the skeppsrået (ship's rå) and gruvrået (mine's rå). Rår may appear as animals or as men or women; the skogsrå and bergsrå are usually described as female.

short_description.en: In folk tradition and in literature the Fairy Queen, or Queen of the Fairies, rules over the fairies, sometimes alongside a king; Titania and Mab are common names.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat dan sastra, Fairy Queen atau Queen of the Fairies adalah penguasa perempuan para peri, kadang tetapi tidak selalu berpasangan dengan seorang raja. Tergantung karyanya, ia bisa bernama atau tanpa nama; Titania dan Mab adalah dua nama yang sering dipakai. Tuatha Dé Danann dan Daoine Sidhe dalam mitologi Irlandia (Irish) memiliki banyak raja dan ratu setempat; Oonagh (Una, Nuala) adalah istri Finvarra, raja peri Irlandia (Ireland) barat. Ratu peri Irlandia lainnya termasuk Clíodhna dari Munster, Aibhell, dan Ainé.
long_description.en: Folk tradition and literature know a Fairy Queen, also called Queen of the Fairies, a woman ruling over the fairies, at times though not always beside a king. Some works name her and some do not; Titania and Mab are two names used often. The Tuatha Dé Danann and Daoine Sidhe of Irish myth had many local kings and queens; Oonagh (Una, Nuala) was wife of Finvarra, fairy king of the west of Ireland. Other Irish fairy queens include Clíodhna of Munster, Aibhell and Ainé.

long_description.id: Tokoh Arthurian Morgan le Fey memerintah pulau gaib Avalon dan kadang digambarkan sebagai ratu peri; dalam Vita Merlini ia Morgen, kepala sembilan ratu bersaudara yang sakti. Ratu peri muncul dalam beberapa Child Ballads: yang baik hati dalam Alison Gross, dan yang kejam dalam Tam Lin, yang membayar upeti kepada Neraka setiap tujuh tahun. Dalam Thomas the Rhymer, ratu peri tanpa nama menjadikan Thomas kekasihnya dan meninggalkannya dengan kemampuan bernubuat. Menurut artikel es, Child Ballads adalah kumpulan 305 balada rakyat dari Inggris (Inglaterra) dan Skotlandia (Escocia) yang dihimpun Francis James Child.
long_description.en: The Arthurian Morgan le Fey ruled the otherworldly island of Avalon and was at times shown as a fairy queen; in the Vita Merlini she is Morgen, head of nine magical sister queens. Fairy queens appear in some Child Ballads: a kindly one in Alison Gross and a cruel one in Tam Lin, who pays a tithe to Hell every seven years. In Thomas the Rhymer an unnamed fairy queen takes Thomas as her lover and leaves him able to prophesy. According to the es article the Child Ballads are a set of 305 folk ballads from England (Inglaterra) and Scotland (Escocia) gathered by Francis James Child.

short_description.id: Turul adalah burung pemangsa mitologis dalam tradisi Hungaria dan Turk, umumnya digambarkan sebagai falkon, dan menjadi lambang nasional bangsa Hungaria.
short_description.en: The Turul is a mythological bird of prey of Hungarian and Turkic tradition, usually shown as a falcon, and a national symbol of the Hungarians.

long_description.id: Turul adalah burung pemangsa mitologis dalam tradisi Hungaria dan Turk yang umumnya digambarkan sebagai falkon, dan kini menjadi lambang nasional bangsa Hungaria. Burung ini kemungkinan besar didasarkan pada falkon besar. Dalam bahasa Hungaria, turul adalah sebutan untuk satu jenis falkon, dan asal katanya kini dianggap paling mungkin dari bahasa Turk, dengan bentuk toġrïl atau toğrul yang berarti burung pemangsa sedang hingga besar dari famili Accipitridae.
long_description.en: The Turul is a mythological bird of prey of Hungarian and Turkic tradition, usually pictured as a falcon, and today a national symbol of the Hungarians. It is probably modelled on a large falcon. In Hungarian, turul named one kind of falcon, and the word is now thought most likely to be of Turkic origin, from toġrïl or toğrul, a medium to large bird of prey of the family Accipitridae.

long_description.id: Dalam legenda Emese yang tercatat dalam Gesta Hungarorum dan Chronicon Pictum, turul muncul dalam mimpi Emese ketika ia sudah hamil. Peran turul di sini adalah roh pelindung yang menjaga bayi Álmos dari bahaya, motif yang sangat mirip dengan peran Simurgh dalam epos Iran Shahnameh. Dalam mimpi kedua pemimpin suku Hungaria, elang-elang lambang bangsa Pecheneg menyerang kuda mereka, lalu turul datang menyelamatkannya.
long_description.en: Both the Gesta Hungarorum and the Chronicon Pictum preserve the tale of Emese, who sees the turul in a dream while already carrying her child. Its role there is that of a guardian spirit shielding the infant Álmos from harm, a motif very close to the Simurgh's role in the Iranian epic Shahnameh. In a second dream of the Hungarian tribal leader, eagles, the emblem of the Pechenegs, attacked their horses and the turul came to rescue them.

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi Hungaria, turul bermula sebagai lambang klan wangsa Árpád yang berkuasa pada abad ke-9 dan ke-10. Gesta Hunnorum et Hungarorum menyebut wangsa itu keturunan klan Turul, dan Gesta Hungarorum mencatat turul sebagai leluhur totemik Árpád. Sepasang cakram perak bermotif turul ditemukan di Rakamaz dari pemakaman Hungaria abad ke-10.
long_description.en: In Hungarian tradition the turul began as the clan emblem of the ruling Árpád dynasty in the 9th and 10th centuries. The Gesta Hunnorum et Hungarorum says the dynasty descended from the Turul clan, and the Gesta Hungarorum records the turul as Árpád's totemic ancestor. A pair of silver discs with a turul motif was found at Rakamaz in a 10th-century Hungarian cemetery.

long_description.id: Kini turul menjadi unsur utama lambang Angkatan Bersenjata Hungaria: burung bersayap terbentang yang mencengkeram pedang Raja Santo Stefanus. Patung turul di sebuah gunung dekat Tatabánya disebut patung burung terbesar di Eropa.
long_description.en: Today the turul is the centrepiece of the Hungarian Defence Forces emblem: a bird with outspread wings gripping the sword of King Saint Stephen. The turul statue on a mountain near Tatabánya is described as the largest bird statue in Europe.

short_description.id: Volkolak adalah manusia serigala dalam mitologi Slavia: penyihir yang sengaja menjadi serigala, orang yang terlahir atau dikutuk berubah wujud, dan korban sihir.
short_description.en: The volkolak is the werewolf of Slavic mythology: a sorcerer who becomes a wolf at will, a person born or cursed to shapeshift, or a victim of witchcraft.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, manusia serigala atau volkolak adalah manusia yang untuk sementara berwujud serigala; ia tampak seperti serigala biasa, tetap berakal manusia, tetapi tidak dapat berbicara. Kepercayaan ini kuno dan dikenal di semua bangsa Slavia, paling rinci di Belarus, Polandia, dan Ukraina; di Rusia istilah volkolak hanya tercatat di selatan, dan Slavia Selatan mencampurnya dengan vampir.
long_description.en: In Slavic mythology the werewolf or volkolak is a person who temporarily becomes a wolf; it looks like an ordinary wolf and keeps a human mind but cannot speak. The belief is ancient and known to all Slavic peoples, most fully among Belarusians, Poles and Ukrainians; among Russians the word volkolak is recorded only in the south, and South Slavic beliefs merge it with the vampire.

long_description.id: Penyihir menjadi serigala dengan mantra dan dengan melompati atau berguling melewati benda bertuah, misalnya pisau yang ditancapkan ke tanah, lalu kembali dengan mengulang secara terbalik. Ada pula yang terlahir atau dikutuk berubah wujud berkala, tidak terkendali dan menyerang ternak serta orang. Korban sihir, seperti rombongan pernikahan dalam kisah populer, menderita dan merindukan hidup manusia.
long_description.en: Sorcerers become wolves by spells and by leaping or tumbling over charmed objects such as knives stuck in the ground, returning by doing it in reverse. Others are born or cursed to change periodically, uncontrolled and attacking livestock and people. Victims of witchcraft, like the wedding party of a popular tale, suffer and long for human life.

long_description.id: Mitos ini mungkin berakar pada kepercayaan totem dan ritus inisiasi pemuda.
long_description.en: The myth may be rooted in totemic beliefs and youth initiation rites.

claims.quote: In Slavic mythology, a werewolf is a human-shapeshifter who temporarily takes the form of a wolf. Werewolves were often described as ordinary wolves, though some accounts noted peculiarities in appearance or behavior that hinted at their human origin. Werewolves retain human intelligence but cannot speak.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, manusia serigala adalah manusia pengubah wujud yang untuk sementara berwujud serigala; ia sering digambarkan seperti serigala biasa dengan beberapa keanehan yang menandakan asal manusianya, tetap berakal manusia tetapi tidak dapat berbicara.
statement.en: In Slavic mythology a werewolf is a human shapeshifter who temporarily takes wolf form; often described as an ordinary wolf with some oddities betraying its human origin, it keeps human intelligence but cannot speak.

claims.quote: The concept is ancient and appears to varying degrees among all Slavic peoples, with the most detailed accounts among Belarusians, Poles, and Ukrainians. In Russian folklore, the character is often simply called a shapeshifter, sharing clear similarities with the werewolf.

statement.id: Konsep ini kuno dan dikenal di semua bangsa Slavia, paling rinci di kalangan orang Belarus, Polandia, dan Ukraina; dalam cerita rakyat Rusia tokoh ini sering disebut pengubah wujud saja.
statement.en: The idea is ancient and found among all Slavic peoples, most fully among Belarusians, Poles and Ukrainians; in Russian folklore the figure is often simply called a shapeshifter.

claims.quote: Among Russians, the term volkolak is recorded only in southern regions

statement.id: Di kalangan orang Rusia, istilah volkolak hanya tercatat di wilayah selatan.
statement.en: Among Russians the term volkolak is recorded only in southern regions.

claims.quote: Ваўкалак, ваўкалака — чалавек, ператвораны ў ваўка, пярэварацень.

statement.id: Dalam bahasa Belarus, vaŭkalak atau vaŭkalaka adalah manusia yang diubah menjadi serigala, sang pengubah wujud.
statement.en: In Belarusian, the vaŭkalak or vaŭkalaka is a person turned into a wolf, a shapeshifter.

claims.quote: It was believed that sorcerers could transform into wolves by reciting spells and performing actions such as leaping, stepping over, tumbling through, or passing through magically imbued objects, or draping them over themselves.

statement.id: Penyihir dipercaya dapat menjadi serigala dengan membaca mantra lalu melompati, melangkahi, berguling melewati, atau menerobos benda bertuah, atau menyampirkannya ke tubuh.
statement.en: Sorcerers were believed to turn into wolves by reciting spells and leaping over, stepping over, tumbling through or passing through charmed objects, or draping them over themselves.

claims.quote: To revert to human form, sorcerers typically needed to repeat the actions in reverse. Sorcerers voluntarily became werewolves to cause harm to others.

statement.id: Untuk kembali menjadi manusia, penyihir mengulang tindakan itu secara terbalik; mereka menjadi manusia serigala dengan sengaja untuk mencelakai orang lain.
statement.en: To turn back into humans, sorcerers repeated the actions in reverse; they became werewolves on purpose to harm others.

claims.quote: Ператварэнне па ўласнай волі адбываецца шляхам перакульвання праз уторкнутыя вастрыём уверх у зямлю нажы (іх колькасць у розных паданнях падаецца ад аднаго да дванаццаці — 1, 5, 7, 12).

statement.id: Menurut kepercayaan Belarus, perubahan sukarela dilakukan dengan berjungkir balik melewati pisau yang ditancapkan ke tanah dengan ujung ke atas, berjumlah antara 1 dan 12 menurut versinya (1, 5, 7, 12).
statement.en: In Belarusian belief, a willed change is made by somersaulting over knives stuck point-up in the ground, from one to twelve in different tales (1, 5, 7, 12).

claims.quote: Some beliefs described people born with a predisposition to periodic shapeshifting due to their parents' actions or as punishment for their own sins. Such werewolves were thought to exhibit zoomorphic traits in human form, such as hair resembling wolf fur.

statement.id: Sebagian kepercayaan menyebut orang yang sejak lahir cenderung berubah wujud secara berkala karena perbuatan orang tuanya atau sebagai hukuman atas dosanya sendiri; dalam wujud manusia mereka punya ciri hewan seperti rambut mirip bulu serigala.
statement.en: Some beliefs told of people born prone to periodic shapeshifting because of their parents' deeds or as punishment for their own sins; in human form they showed animal traits such as wolf-like hair.

claims.quote: These werewolves were believed to lack control in wolf form, attacking livestock and even humans, including loved ones, and were sometimes associated with cannibalism. Ancient beliefs linked werewolves to celestial events like eclipses.

statement.id: Manusia serigala jenis ini dipercaya tidak dapat mengendalikan diri dalam wujud serigala, menyerang ternak bahkan manusia, termasuk orang terkasih, dan kadang dikaitkan dengan kanibalisme; kepercayaan kuno juga mengaitkannya dengan gerhana.
statement.en: Such werewolves were thought to lose control in wolf form, attacking livestock and even people, loved ones included, and were sometimes tied to cannibalism; ancient beliefs also linked them with eclipses.

claims.quote: Folk beliefs also held that sorcerers or witches could transform a person into a wolf, often as an act of revenge, by casting spells on a wolf skin, belt, or enchanted door, among other methods. A popular narrative involved transforming an entire wedding party into wolves.

statement.id: Penyihir laki-laki atau perempuan juga dipercaya dapat mengubah seseorang menjadi serigala, sering sebagai balas dendam, dengan memantrai kulit serigala, sabuk, atau pintu; kisah populer menceritakan seluruh rombongan pernikahan diubah menjadi serigala.
statement.en: Sorcerers or witches were also believed able to turn a person into a wolf, often in revenge, by bewitching a wolf skin, a belt or a door; a popular tale has a whole wedding party turned into wolves.

claims.quote: Involuntary werewolves suffered fear and despair, longing for human life and avoiding true wolves. They were thought to avoid carrion and raw meat, subsisting on foraged food or stolen human provisions.

statement.id: Manusia serigala yang terpaksa menderita ketakutan dan putus asa, merindukan hidup sebagai manusia, menjauhi serigala sejati, dan menghindari bangkai serta daging mentah.
statement.en: Involuntary werewolves suffered fear and despair, longed for human life, avoided real wolves and shunned carrion and raw meat.

claims.quote: The myth likely originated from ancient totemic beliefs and rites of youthful initiation. The werewolf image may have been influenced by observations of people with physical or mental disorders or of old and sick wolves.

statement.id: Mitos ini kemungkinan berasal dari kepercayaan totem kuno dan ritus inisiasi pemuda, dan citranya mungkin dipengaruhi pengamatan terhadap orang dengan gangguan fisik atau jiwa atau serigala tua dan sakit.
statement.en: The myth probably grew from ancient totemic beliefs and youth initiation rites, and its image may reflect observations of people with physical or mental disorders or of old, sick wolves.

claims.quote: Южнославянские представления смешивают волколаков с упырями (вампирами).

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Rusia, kepercayaan Slavia Selatan mencampuradukkan volkolak dengan upir (vampir).
statement.en: According to the Russian article, South Slavic beliefs conflate volkolaks with upirs (vampires).

short_description.id: Lutin adalah makhluk kecil jenaka sejenis hobgoblin dalam cerita rakyat Prancis, yang perannya mirip roh rumah tangga dan kepercayaannya juga menyebar ke Quebec.
short_description.en: The lutin is a small, mischievous hobgoblin of French folklore, similar to a household spirit, whose belief also spread to Quebec.

long_description.id: Lutin adalah sejenis hobgoblin jenaka dalam cerita rakyat dan dongeng Prancis: makhluk kecil mirip manusia yang aktif di malam hari, terutama dikenal di Berry, Normandia, dan Picardie. Di Normandia perannya mirip roh rumah tangga di Inggris, Jerman, dan Skandinavia, sedangkan Ardennes dan Wallonia mengenal roh serupa bernama nuton.
long_description.en: The lutin is a mischievous hobgoblin of French folklore and fairy tales: a small nocturnal humanoid known especially in Berry, Normandy and Picardy. In Normandy it plays a role like the household spirits of England, Germany and Scandinavia, while the Ardennes and Wallonia know a similar spirit called the nuton.

long_description.id: Lutin kadang menjelma kuda berpelana yang disebut Le Cheval Bayard, dan suka menjalin rambut orang atau kuda hingga kusut. Dalam dongeng Le Prince Lutin karya Marie Catherine d'Aulnoy (1697), lutin dapat menjadi tak terlihat sesuka hati dan melintasi alam semesta dalam sekejap.
long_description.en: The lutin sometimes becomes a saddled horse called Le Cheval Bayard and likes to tangle the hair of people or horses. In Marie Catherine d'Aulnoy's fairy tale Le Prince Lutin (1697), the lutin can become invisible at will and cross the universe in a moment.

long_description.id: Namanya tercatat sebagai netun sekitar 1176–1181 dalam karya Chrétien de Troyes dan berasal dari Neptunus, nama dewa laut Romawi. Kepercayaan pada lutin juga menyebar ke Quebec, Kanada, tempat lutin dipercaya berwujud hewan peliharaan; kucing yang seluruhnya putih terutama dicurigai sebagai lutin.
long_description.en: The name is attested as netun around 1176–1181 in Chrétien de Troyes and comes from Neptunus, the Roman sea god's name. Belief in lutins also spread to Quebec, Canada, where they were thought to take the form of pets; completely white cats were especially suspected of being lutins.
