short_description.id: Girt Dog of Ennerdale adalah anjing misterius yang diyakini membantai ratusan domba di perbukitan Cumberland, Inggris, pada 1810 dan kini menjadi sosok legendaris setempat.
short_description.en: The Girt Dog of Ennerdale was a mysterious dog believed to have slaughtered hundreds of sheep in the fells of Cumberland, England, in 1810, and is now a local legendary figure.

long_description.id: Girt Dog of Ennerdale, juga disebut Vampire Dog atau Demon Dog of Ennerdale, diyakini membunuh antara 300 dan 400 domba di perbukitan Cumberland antara Mei dan September 1810. Kata "girt" dalam dialek Cumbria berarti besar. Anjing ini masih dikenang sebagai sosok legendaris di daerah Ennerdale.
long_description.en: The Girt Dog of Ennerdale, also called the Vampire Dog or Demon Dog of Ennerdale, reportedly slaughtered somewhere from 300 to 400 sheep on the Cumberland fells from May to September 1810. "Girt" is Cumbrian for great. The dog is still remembered as a legendary figure in the Ennerdale district.

long_description.id: Ia pertama kali terlihat oleh Mr Mossop dari Thornholme pada 10 Mei 1810. Anjing berbulu licin ini berwarna cokelat tikus dengan belang gelap seperti harimau dan beratnya delapan stone. Asalnya tidak jelas; ada yang mengira ia kabur dari rombongan gipsi, ada pula yang menduga ia persilangan mastiff dan greyhound.
long_description.en: It was first seen by Mr Mossop of Thornholme on 10 May 1810. The smooth-haired dog was tawny mouse-coloured with dark tiger-like streaks and weighed eight stones. Its origin was unclear; some thought it had escaped from a gipsy troop, others that it was a mastiff and greyhound cross.

long_description.id: Anjing itu biasanya berburu pada malam hari dan sering membunuh tujuh atau delapan domba dalam semalam; menurut satu cerita ia meminum darah langsung dari leher korbannya. Ia tidak pernah terdengar menggonggong atau melolong, mengabaikan umpan beracun, dan membawa para pengejarnya berlari puluhan mil tanpa hasil.
long_description.en: The dog usually hunted at night and often killed seven or eight sheep in one night; by one account it drank blood straight from its victims' necks. It was never heard to bark or howl, ignored poisoned bait, and led its pursuers on fruitless chases of many miles.

long_description.id: John Russell menawarkan hadiah £10 untuk anjing itu, hidup atau mati. Pada 12 September 1810 John Steel menembaknya di Eskett Woods dekat Rowrah dan menerima hadiah tersebut. Kulit awetannya kemudian dipamerkan di museum di Keswick sebelum dibuang karena rusak.
long_description.en: John Russell offered a £10 reward for the dog, dead or alive. On 12 September 1810 John Steel shot it in Eskett Woods near Rowrah and received the reward. Its stuffed skin was later displayed in a museum at Keswick before being discarded as it decayed.

short_description.id: Dunnie adalah makhluk kecil sejenis Brownie dari cerita rakyat Northumberland yang gemar menyamar sebagai kuda lalu menghilang, dan sering dianggap hantu seorang perampok perbatasan.
short_description.en: The Dunnie is a small Brownie-type being of Northumberland folklore who likes to pose as a horse and then vanish, and is often thought to be the ghost of a border reiver.

long_description.id: Dunnie adalah makhluk kecil mirip Brownie dalam cerita rakyat perbatasan Inggris-Skotlandia, khususnya Northumberland. Yang paling terkenal adalah Dunnie dari Hazlerigg (dalam catatan Henderson ditulis Haselrigg) di paroki Chatton. Henderson menulis bahwa seperti makhluk sejenisnya, Dunnie sangat gemar melakukan tipu daya yang jahil dan merepotkan.
long_description.en: Folklore of the Anglo-Scottish borders, Northumberland in particular, tells of the Dunnie, a little creature much like a Brownie. The best known is the Dunnie of Hazlerigg (spelled Haselrigg by Henderson) in the parish of Chatton. Henderson says that, as with the rest of its kind, the Dunnie loves playing troublesome pranks.

long_description.id: Tipuan khasnya adalah menyamar sebagai kuda. Ketika seorang petani hendak menjemput bidan, Dunnie mengambil wujud kudanya, membawa keduanya dengan selamat, lalu tiba-tiba lenyap di bagian jalan paling berlumpur. Ia juga menyamar sebagai kuda bajak: begitu dipasangi tali kekang, tali itu jatuh ke tanah dan sang kuda berlari kencang melintasi daerah itu.
long_description.en: His typical trick is posing as a horse. When a farmer sets out to fetch the midwife, the Dunnie takes the form of his horse, carries them both safely, then suddenly vanishes in the muddiest part of the road. He also poses as a plough-horse: once harnessed, the harness falls to the ground and the horse races off across the country.

long_description.id: Dunnie juga dikatakan berkeliaran di tebing Cheviots sambil mengulang-ulang sebuah bait dengan suara sedih tentang harta di Cockenheugh dan Collierheugh serta kunci yang hilang. Dari lagu itu muncul anggapan bahwa Dunnie sebenarnya hantu seorang perampok perbatasan (reiver) yang menimbun jarahannya di sana dan terus menjaganya. Seorang kawan Henderson bahkan menunjuk bagian batu paling curam di Haselrigg sebagai tempat Dunnie biasa duduk di malam hari.
long_description.en: The Dunnie was also said to wander the crags of the Cheviots, repeating in a melancholy voice a verse about treasure at Cockenheugh and Collierheugh and a lost key. From this song came the idea that the Dunnie is really the ghost of a reiver who hoarded his loot there and still guards it. A friend of Henderson's even pointed to the steepest rocks at Haselrigg as the place where the Dunnie used to sit at night.

short_description.id: Uylak adalah penyihir atau roh jahat dalam cerita rakyat Turkik yang terkait dengan Iblis, dapat berubah wujud, dan mengganggu orang di jalan sepi.
short_description.en: An Uylak is an evil witch or spirit of Turkic folklore linked to the Devil, able to change shape and pester people on lonely roads.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Turkik, Uylak adalah penyihir atau roh, lelaki maupun perempuan, yang dianggap jahat dan terkait dengan Iblis. Ia mencelakai manusia dengan mengirim penyakit, membunuh ternak, dan merusak panen, serta mengganggu dan menakuti orang di jalan-jalan sepi. Uylak dapat menjelma anjing, kucing, peti mati, atau bahkan manusia, dan tahan terhadap sihir Archura.
long_description.en: In Turkic folklore an Uylak is a witch or spirit, male or female, considered evil and linked to the Devil. It harms people by sending illness, killing cattle and spoiling harvests, and pesters and frightens travellers on lonely roads. An Uylak can become a hound, a cat, a coffin or even a human, and resists Archura's spells.

long_description.id: Namanya berasal dari kata kerja Turki uylamak, "mendesak, mengganggu", dan oyalamak, "menunda", dan kata ini juga dipakai sebagai makian.
long_description.en: Its name comes from the Turkish verbs uylamak, "to insist, pester", and oyalamak, "to delay", and the word is also used as an insult.

short_description.id: Rokita adalah iblis dalam cerita rakyat Polandia yang mendiami rawa, hutan, dan pohon dedalu tua, sangat kuat tetapi tidak terlalu cerdik.
short_description.en: Rokita is a devil of Polish folklore dwelling in bogs, forests and old willow trees, very strong but not very cunning.

long_description.id: Rokita adalah iblis dalam cerita rakyat Polandia yang konon mendiami gerbang ke dunia bawah: lahan basah, hutan, dan bagian dalam pohon dedalu tua. Ia sangat kuat tetapi tidak terlalu cerdik. Di Łęczyca ia sering disamakan dengan Boruta dan digambarkan sebagai jenderal bermantel emas, serta bisa muncul sebagai babi, burung, ikan, kuda, anjing, tikus, atau kucing, selalu dengan niat jahat terhadap manusia.
long_description.en: Rokita is a devil of Polish folklore said to inhabit gateways to the underworld: wetlands, forests and the insides of old willow trees. He is enormously strong but not very cunning. In Łęczyca he is often equated with Boruta and shown as a general in a golden cloak, and he can appear as a pig, bird, fish, horse, dog, mouse or cat, always hostile to people.

long_description.id: Dalam satu versi ia disebut Rokietnik, jiwa jahat penghuni rawa yang menenggelamkan penyusup. Legenda lain mengisahkannya minum bir bersama Boruta di sebuah kedai di Łódź, atau meminjamkan uang tanpa bunga kepada petani miskin dengan jiwa sebagai jaminan. Para penyihir juga memohon kepadanya agar sapi memberi lebih banyak susu.
long_description.en: In one version he is called Rokietnik, an evil bog-dwelling soul who drowns intruders. Other legends have him drinking beer with Boruta at an inn in Łódź, or lending a poor peasant money without interest against his soul. Witches also prayed to him for cows that gave more milk.

short_description.id: Muroni adalah vampir dalam mitologi Wallachia yang bisa berubah menjadi berbagai hewan; namanya ubahan Inggris lama dari moroi Rumania.
short_description.en: The Muroni is a vampire of Wallachian mythology able to turn into various animals; its name is an old English corruption of the Romanian moroi.

long_description.id: Muroni atau Murony adalah vampir dalam mitologi Wallachia. Ia mampu berubah menjadi berbagai hewan, sehingga serangannya sering dikira serangan hewan, dan satu-satunya tanda kehadirannya adalah kehilangan darah yang luar biasa. Muroni dipercaya sebenarnya hantu pengisap darah yang mengambil wujud makhluk lain agar mudah memangsa.
long_description.en: The Muroni or Murony is a vampire of Wallachian mythology. It could turn into various animals, so its attacks were often taken for animal attacks, the only sign of its presence being exceptional blood loss. It was believed to be really a blood-sucking ghost that took other forms to feed more easily.

long_description.id: Nama murony dan muroni adalah bentuk ubahan Inggris lama dari istilah Rumania moroi, yang terutama dipakai dalam dialek selatan seperti di Wallachia. Moroi berbeda dari strigoi karena fana, tetapi bila dibunuh strigoi ia menjadi strigoi yang abadi. Ia bisa berubah menjadi anjing, kucing, kodok, atau serangga, dan hanya bisa dimusnahkan dengan menggali jasadnya, menusuk dahi dengan jarum, menancapkan pasak kayu ke jantung, lalu membakarnya.
long_description.en: The names murony and muroni are old English corruptions of the Romanian term moroi, used mostly in southern dialects such as in Wallachia. The moroi differs from the strigoi in being mortal, but if killed by a strigoi it becomes an immortal strigoi. It can turn into a dog, cat, toad or insects, and could be destroyed only by digging up the body, driving a needle into the forehead, staking the heart and burning it.

who.en: The Muroni is a shapeshifting vampire.

Due to this characteristic, a Muroni attack could be very hard to identify and could often be thought of as an animal attack. The only sign that a Muroni was there at all was an exceptional amount of blood loss.

statement.id: Muroni (atau Murony) adalah vampir dalam mitologi Wallachia yang mampu berubah menjadi berbagai hewan, sehingga serangannya sulit dikenali dan sering dikira serangan hewan; satu-satunya tanda kehadirannya adalah kehilangan darah yang luar biasa banyak.
statement.en: The Muroni (or Murony) is a vampire of Wallachian mythology able to transform into various animals, so its attacks were hard to identify and often taken for animal attacks; the only sign of its presence was an exceptional loss of blood.

claims.quote: The Muroni is one of many vampire legends which was believed to be a blood-sucking ghost in reality, only taking on the form of other beings to make feeding easier.

statement.id: Muroni termasuk legenda vampir yang dipercaya sebenarnya hantu pengisap darah, yang hanya mengambil wujud makhluk lain agar lebih mudah memangsa.
statement.en: The Muroni is one of many vampire legends believed to be really a blood-sucking ghost, taking other forms only to make feeding easier.

claims.quote: Murony ou muroni sont des déformations anglaises anciennes du terme roumain moroï, proche mais différent des strigoï : il est mortel alors que le strigoï est immortel, mais si un moroï est tué par un strigoï, il devient strigoï et immortel à son tour.

statement.id: Murony atau muroni adalah bentuk ubahan Inggris lama dari istilah Rumania moroi, yang dekat tetapi berbeda dari strigoi: moroi fana sedangkan strigoi abadi, tetapi bila moroi dibunuh strigoi ia menjadi strigoi yang abadi pula.
statement.en: Murony or muroni are old English corruptions of the Romanian term moroi, close to but distinct from the strigoi: it is mortal while the strigoi is immortal, but if a moroi is killed by a strigoi it becomes an immortal strigoi in turn.

claims.quote: Elles ne pouvaient être détruites que si leur corps était déterré, qu’on leur enfonce une aiguille dans le front et qu’on transperce leur cœur avec un pieu en bois avant de les brûler.

statement.id: Makhluk-makhluk ini hanya bisa dimusnahkan bila jasadnya digali, dahinya ditusuk jarum, dan jantungnya ditembus pasak kayu sebelum dibakar.
statement.en: These creatures could be destroyed only if their body was dug up, a needle driven into the forehead and the heart pierced with a wooden stake before burning.

claims.quote: Le moroi peut se métamorphoser en chien, en chat, en crapaud, en grenouille, en puce, en pou, en punaise ou en araignée.

statement.id: Moroi bisa berubah menjadi anjing, kucing, kodok, katak, kutu loncat, kutu rambut, kepinding, atau laba-laba.
statement.en: The moroi can turn into a dog, cat, toad, frog, flea, louse, bedbug or spider.

claims.quote: Moroï est plutôt utilisé dans les parlers roumains méridionaux, notamment en Valachie

statement.id: Kata moroi lebih banyak dipakai dalam dialek Rumania selatan, terutama di Wallachia.
statement.en: The word moroi is used mostly in southern Romanian dialects, notably in Wallachia.

short_description.id: Sigmund adalah pahlawan saga Völsunga, satu-satunya yang dapat mencabut pedang Gram dari pohon Barnstokk, yang sempat hidup sebagai manusia serigala dan menjadi ayah Sigurð.
short_description.en: Sigmund is the hero of the Völsunga saga, the only one able to pull the sword Gram from the tree Barnstokk, who lived for a time as a werewolf and fathered Sigurð.

long_description.id: Sigmund adalah pahlawan mitologi Jermanik dalam saga Völsunga, putra Völsung dan ayah Sigurð si pembunuh naga. Ia satu-satunya yang mampu mencabut pedang Gram yang ditancapkan Odin ke pohon Barnstokk. Setelah ayahnya dibunuh Siggeir dan saudara-saudaranya dimangsa serigala betina, ia selamat dengan menggigit lidah serigala itu.
long_description.en: Sigmund is a hero of Germanic myth in the Völsunga saga, son of Völsung and father of Sigurð the dragon-slayer. He alone could pull the sword Gram that Odin had thrust into the tree Barnstokk. After Siggeir killed his father and a she-wolf devoured his brothers, he survived by biting off the wolf's tongue.

long_description.id: Bersama putranya Sinfjötli, yang lahir dari saudarinya Signý, ia hidup sebagai buronan, sempat menjadi manusia serigala, lalu membunuh Siggeir. Ia juga disebut dalam Beowulf dan kisahnya diadaptasi dalam opera Die Walküre karya Richard Wagner.
long_description.en: With his son Sinfjötli, born of his sister Signý, he lived as an outlaw, for a time as a werewolf, and then killed Siggeir. He is also mentioned in Beowulf and his story is adapted in Richard Wagner's opera Die Walküre.

note.en: His son, the dragon-slayer.
His sister.
The god who gave him the sword Gram.

description.id: Opera yang mengadaptasi kisahnya.
description.en: An opera adapting his story.

claims.quote: In Germanic mythology, Sigmund (Old Norse: Sigmundr [ˈsiɣˌmundz̠], Old English: Sigemund) is a hero whose story is told in the Völsunga saga.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Jermanik, Sigmund (Norse Kuno: Sigmundr; Inggris Kuno: Sigemund) adalah pahlawan yang kisahnya diceritakan dalam saga Völsunga.
statement.en: In Germanic mythology Sigmund (Old Norse Sigmundr, Old English Sigemund) is a hero whose story is told in the Völsunga saga.

claims.quote: He and his sister, Signý, are the children of Völsung and his wife Hljod. Sigmund is best known as the father of Sigurð the dragon-slayer

statement.id: Ia dan saudarinya Signý adalah anak Völsung dan istrinya Hljod, dan Sigmund paling dikenal sebagai ayah Sigurð si pembunuh naga.
statement.en: He and his sister Signý are the children of Völsung and his wife Hljod, and Sigmund is best known as the father of Sigurð the dragon-slayer.

claims.quote: when Odin, disguised as a beggar, plunges a sword (Gram) into the living tree Barnstokk ("offspring-trunk") around which Völsung's hall is built. The disguised Odin announces that the man who can remove the sword will have it as a gift. Only Sigmund is able to free the sword from the tree.

statement.id: Odin yang menyamar sebagai pengemis menancapkan pedang Gram ke pohon Barnstokk di tengah balairung Völsung dan menyatakan siapa pun yang mencabutnya boleh memilikinya; hanya Sigmund yang berhasil.
statement.en: Odin, disguised as a beggar, thrusts the sword Gram into the tree Barnstokk in Völsung's hall, saying whoever pulls it out may keep it; only Sigmund succeeds.

claims.quote: When the Völsung clan arrive, they are attacked by the Gauts; King Völsung is killed and his sons captured.

statement.id: Ketika klan Völsung datang ke Gautland, mereka diserang orang Gaut; Raja Völsung tewas dan putra-putranya ditawan.
statement.en: When the Völsungs arrive in Gautland they are attacked by the Gauts; King Völsung is killed and his sons captured.

claims.quote: On the ninth night, she has a servant smear honey on Sigmund's face and when the she-wolf arrives, she starts licking the honey off and sticks her tongue into Sigmund's mouth, whereupon Sigmund bites her tongue off, killing her.

statement.id: Setelah serigala betina jelmaan ibu Siggeir memangsa saudara-saudaranya satu per satu, pada malam kesembilan Signý menyuruh pelayan mengoleskan madu ke wajah Sigmund; ketika serigala itu menjilat dan memasukkan lidahnya ke mulut Sigmund, ia menggigit putus lidahnya.
statement.en: After the she-wolf, Siggeir's shapeshifting mother, devours his brothers one by one, on the ninth night Signý has honey smeared on Sigmund's face; when the wolf licks it and puts her tongue in his mouth, he bites it off and kills her.

claims.quote: Mit seiner Zwillingsschwester Signy zeugte er einen Sohn Sinfiötli, mit dem zusammen er den Mord an seinem Vater Wölsung rächte.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, bersama saudari kembarnya Signy ia memperoleh putra Sinfjötli, yang bersamanya membalas pembunuhan Völsung.
statement.en: According to the German article, with his twin sister Signy he fathered Sinfjötli, with whom he avenged Völsung's murder.

claims.quote: Die beiden lebten als Geächtete, erlebten einige Abenteuer, zwischenzeitlich auch als Werwölfe, bis es ihnen gelang ihren Vater/Großvater Wölsung zu rächen, indem sie Siggeir töteten.

statement.id: Keduanya hidup sebagai buronan, sempat menjadi manusia serigala, sampai berhasil membalas dendam dengan membunuh Siggeir.
statement.en: The two lived as outlaws, for a time as werewolves, until they avenged Völsung by killing Siggeir.

claims.quote: Il apparaît notamment dans la Völsunga saga, la Þiðrekssaga, et est également mentionné dans le poème anglo-saxon Beowulf sous le nom de Sigemund. Une adaptation de son histoire apparaît dans l'opéra La Walkyrie (Die Walküre) du cycle de L'Anneau du Nibelung (Der Ring des Nibelungen), de Richard Wagner.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, ia muncul dalam saga Völsunga dan Þiðrekssaga, disebut sebagai Sigemund dalam Beowulf, dan kisahnya diadaptasi dalam opera Die Walküre dari siklus Der Ring des Nibelungen karya Richard Wagner.
statement.en: According to the French article, he appears in the Völsunga saga and Þiðrekssaga, is named Sigemund in Beowulf, and his story is adapted in the opera Die Walküre of Richard Wagner's Ring cycle.

short_description.id: Duppy adalah sebutan Karibia untuk hantu atau roh, umumnya dianggap roh jahat yang membawa kemalangan dan menghantui orang pada malam hari.
short_description.en: Duppy is the Caribbean word for a ghost or spirit, generally seen as a malevolent spirit that brings misfortune and haunts people at night.

long_description.id: Duppy adalah kata asal Afrika yang dipakai di pulau-pulau Karibia seperti Bahama, Barbados, dan Jamaika untuk hantu atau roh; di banyak pulau Antilles Kecil roh ini disebut jumbie. Duppy umumnya dianggap roh jahat yang membawa kemalangan dan menghantui orang pada malam hari. Rolling Calf yang berbelit rantai, kuda berkaki tiga, dan Ol' Hige termasuk roh yang paling jahat.
long_description.en: Duppy is a word of African origin used on Caribbean islands such as the Bahamas, Barbados and Jamaica for a ghost or spirit; on many islands of the Lesser Antilles these spirits are called jumbies. Duppy are generally seen as malevolent spirits that bring misfortune and haunt people at night. The chained Rolling Calf, the three-footed horse and Ol' Hige are among the most malicious.

long_description.id: Asal katanya diperdebatkan: dari bahasa Ga, mengingat banyak tradisi Afrika di Jamaika berasal dari orang Ashanti; dari Dapaa, hari khusus dalam kalender Akan; atau dari kata patois Jamaika yang asal-usulnya tidak pasti.
long_description.en: Its origin is debated: from the Ga language, since much African tradition in Jamaica comes from the Ashanti; from Dapaa, a special day in the Akan calendar; or from a Jamaican patois word of uncertain origin.

claims.quote: Duppy are generally regarded as malevolent spirits who bring misfortune and woe on those they set upon. They are said to mostly come out and haunt people at night, and people from around the islands claim to have seen them.

statement.id: Duppy umumnya dianggap roh jahat yang membawa kemalangan; mereka terutama keluar dan menghantui orang pada malam hari.

claims.quote: In many of the islands of the Lesser Antilles, duppy are known as jumbies.

claims.quote: The word duppy originates from the Ga language as most of the African folklore and culture in Jamaica comes from the Ashanti people

short_description.id: Yekyua atau "hewan induk" adalah roh pendamping berwujud hewan yang melindungi dukun Yakut, dan nasib dukun terikat pada hewannya.
short_description.en: A yekyua or "mother animal" is an animal-shaped familiar spirit protecting Yakut shamans, whose fate is bound to their animal.

long_description.id: Dalam kepercayaan Yakut, yekyua atau "hewan induk" adalah golongan roh yang bersembunyi sampai salju mencair pada musim semi. Setiap yekyua terkait dengan seekor hewan dan menjadi roh pendamping yang melindungi dukun; yang paling berbahaya melekat pada dukun perempuan. Hanya dukun yang dapat melihatnya.
long_description.en: In Yakut belief a yekyua or "mother animal" is a class of spirit that hides until the snow melts in spring. Each yekyua is tied to an animal and acts as a familiar that protects a shaman; the most dangerous belong to female shamans. Only shamans can see them.

short_description.id: Lavellan adalah makhluk air dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia, mirip hewan pengerat atau kadal, yang dipercaya berbisa dan membahayakan ternak, bahkan dari kejauhan.
short_description.en: The lavellan is a water creature of Scottish folklore, rodent- or lizard-like, believed to be venomous and harmful to cattle, even from a distance.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia, lavellan atau làbh-allan digambarkan sebagai makhluk mirip hewan pengerat atau kadal dengan gigitan berbisa. Ia dikabarkan tinggal di perairan dan muncul dalam kisah-kisah dari Sutherland dan Caithness. Robert Sibbald dalam Scotia Illustrata menyebutnya hewan yang umum di Caithness, hidup di air, dengan kepala dan warna seperti musang, serta napas yang mencelakakan.
long_description.en: Scottish folklore pictures the lavellan (làbh-allan) as a beast resembling a rodent or a lizard, whose bite carries venom. It reportedly lives in water and features in tales from Sutherland and Caithness. Robert Sibbald's Scotia Illustrata called it an animal common in Caithness, living in water, with a weasel-like head and colouring and a harmful breath.

long_description.id: Penduduk setempat percaya lavellan sangat berbahaya bagi ternak, dan Campbell mencatat bahwa ia konon dapat mencelakai sapi dari jarak empat puluh yard. Sebagai obat, ternak yang sakit diberi minum air tempat kulit lavellan dicelupkan; teks Latin Sibbald menyebut air rebusan kepalanya. Penyair Sutherland, Rob Donn, juga menyebut lavellan dalam lagu satirnya sebagai bahaya bagi orang yang pergi ke rawa atau hutan.
long_description.en: Local people believed the lavellan was especially harmful to cattle, and Campbell recorded that it was said to hurt cattle from forty yards away. As a cure, sick beasts were given water in which a lavellan's skin had been dipped; Sibbald's Latin text speaks of water in which its head was boiled. The Sutherland bard Rob Donn also named the lavellan in a satirical song as a danger to anyone who went to moss or wood.

long_description.id: Thomas Pennant, yang menanyakan makhluk ini di Ausdale, menduga lavellan sebenarnya cerurut air dan menyamakannya dengan hewan yang di Sutherland disebut water mole. Menurut peneliti Lee Raye, pandangan Pennant ini kini umumnya diterima sebagai tepat.
long_description.en: Thomas Pennant, who asked about the creature at Ausdale, suspected that the lavellan was really the water shrew and equated it with the animal called the water mole in Sutherland. The researcher Lee Raye notes that most now accept Pennant's identification as correct.

statement.id: Robert Sibbald dalam Scotia Illustrata menggambarkan lavellan sebagai hewan yang umum di Caithness, tinggal di air, berkepala dan berwarna seperti musang (weasel), dan napasnya mencelakakan.
statement.en: Robert Sibbald's Scotia Illustrata described the lavellan as an animal common in Caithness that stays in water, with a head and colouring like a weasel, whose breath does harm.

statement.en: At the settlement of Ausdale Thomas Pennant asked local people about the lavellan; they believed it was particularly harmful to cattle.

claims.quote: Lavellan.—This animal is peculiar to the north, where it is said to be able to hurt cattle from a distance of forty yards

statement.id: Campbell menulis bahwa lavellan khas wilayah utara dan dikatakan mampu mencelakai ternak dari jarak empat puluh yard.
statement.en: Campbell writes that the lavellan is peculiar to the north, where it is said to hurt cattle from forty yards away.

claims.quote: Lavellan, animal in Cathanesia frequens, in aquis degit, capite mustelae sylvestri simile, ejusdemque coloris, bestia est. Halitu Bestiis nocet.

statement.id: Teks Latin Sibbald yang dikutip Campbell: lavellan (Lavellan) adalah hewan yang umum di Caithness (Cathanesia), hidup di air (in aquis), berkepala seperti musang (mustelae), dan napasnya (halitu) mencelakai hewan ternak.
statement.en: Sibbald's Latin, quoted by Campbell: the Lavellan is an animal common in Caithness (Cathanesia), living in water (in aquis), with a head like a weasel (mustelae), harming beasts with its breath (halitu).

claims.quote: Remedium autem est, si de aqua bibant in quâ ejus caput coctum est.

statement.id: Menurut teks Latin itu, obatnya (remedium) adalah bila ternak minum air (aqua) tempat kepala (caput) hewan itu direbus.
statement.en: According to the Latin text, the remedy (remedium) is for the beasts to drink water (aqua) in which its head (caput) has been boiled.

claims.quote: I inquired here after the Lavellan, which, from description, I suspect to be the water shrew mouse.

statement.en: Pennant wrote that he inquired after the Lavellan and from the description suspected it to be the water shrew mouse.

statement.en: Country people thought it noxious to cattle; they kept its skin and, as a cure for sick beasts, gave them water in which it had been dipped.

claims.quote: I believe it to be the same animal which, in Sutherland, is called the water mole.

statement.id: Pennant meyakini hewan ini sama dengan yang di Sutherland disebut tikus mondok air (water mole).
statement.en: Pennant believed it to be the same animal called the water mole in Sutherland.

claims.quote: It is also mentioned by Rob Donn, the Sutherland bard, in his satirical song on “Mac Rorie’s Breeches”: “Let him not go away from the houses, to moss or wood, lest the Lavellan come and smite him.”

short_description.id: Vâlvă adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Rumania yang berjalan di puncak bukit pada malam hari; ada yang baik (Vâlve Putih) dan ada yang jahat (Vâlve Hitam), dan banyak jenisnya menjaga tempat atau harta tertentu.
short_description.en: The vâlvă is a female spirit of Romanian folklore who walks the hilltops at night; some are good (White Vâlve) and some evil (Black Vâlve), and many kinds guard particular places or treasures.

long_description.id: Vâlvă adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Rumania yang dipercaya berjalan di puncak bukit pada malam hari. Ada Vâlve Albe yang baik dan Vâlve Negre yang jahat. Mereka sering tampil sebagai perempuan, tetapi bisa juga muncul sebagai bayangan atau kucing hitam, dan dapat melindungi desa dari badai, hujan es, dan angin topan.
long_description.en: The vâlvă is a female spirit of Romanian folklore believed to walk the hilltops at night. There are the good Vâlve Albe and the evil Vâlve Negre. They often appear as women but may also come as shadows or black cats, and they can protect a village from storm, hail and hurricane.

long_description.id: Vâlve terbagi dalam banyak jenis menurut apa yang mereka jaga. Vâlva Apei melindungi mata air dan pancuran, Vâlva Comorilor menjaga harta dan bisa menunjukkan tempat harta terkubur, dan Vâlva Ciumei menguasai wabah sampar serta penyakit lain. Vâlva Băilor melindungi tambang; kepergiannya menandakan bijih akan habis.
long_description.en: The vâlve fall into many kinds according to what they guard. Vâlva Apei protects water sources and fountains, Vâlva Comorilor guards treasures and can reveal where they are buried, and Vâlva Ciumei controls plague and other diseases. Vâlva Băilor protects mines; her departure signals that the ore is running out.

long_description.id: Ada pula pandangan lain: vâlve adalah anak-anak yang dikandung pada hari raya besar dan lahir dengan semacam topi kecil berwarna merah di kepala. Para solomonar pun konon termasuk Vâlve, orang-orang berbeda yang memiliki kekuatan istimewa.
long_description.en: Another view holds that vâlve are children conceived on great feast days and born with a small red cap on the head. The solomonari, too, are said to be Vâlve, different people with special powers.

who.en: The vâlvă is a female spirit.

origin.id: Ia berasal dari cerita rakyat Rumania.

role.id: Banyak vâlve menjaga tempat tertentu seperti mata air, tambang, atau harta.
role.en: Many vâlve guard particular places such as springs, mines or treasure.

famous_for.id: Ia terbagi menjadi Vâlve Putih yang baik dan Vâlve Hitam yang jahat.
famous_for.en: They are divided into good White Vâlve and evil Black Vâlve.

did_you_know.id: Menurut kepercayaan, jika Vâlva Băilor meninggalkan sebuah tambang, bijih di tambang itu akan segera habis.
did_you_know.en: According to belief, if Vâlva Băilor leaves a mine, its ore will soon run out.

claims.quote: Vâlvă (plural vâlve) is a female spirit mentioned in the Romanian folklore. The Vâlve are believed to walk over the hilltops at night, and are subdivided into Vâlve Albe ("White Vâlve"), who are considered beneficial, and Vâlve Negre ("Black Vâlve" or "Dark Vâlve"), who are considered evil.

statement.id: Vâlvă (jamak vâlve) adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Rumania yang dipercaya berjalan di puncak-puncak bukit pada malam hari; mereka terbagi menjadi Vâlve Albe ("Vâlve Putih") yang baik dan Vâlve Negre ("Vâlve Hitam") yang jahat.
statement.en: Vâlvă (plural vâlve) is a female spirit of Romanian folklore believed to walk over the hilltops at night; they are divided into the beneficial Vâlve Albe ("White Vâlve") and the evil Vâlve Negre ("Black Vâlve").

claims.quote: They may also appear under various guises, such as shadows or black cats. They also have the ability to shapeshift.

statement.id: Mereka bisa muncul dalam berbagai wujud, seperti bayangan atau kucing hitam, dan mampu berubah wujud.
statement.en: They may appear in various guises, such as shadows or black cats, and can shapeshift.

claims.quote: Vâlva Băilor ("of the mines"), defender and protector of mines and tunnels, whose departure means that the deposit is coming to an end

statement.id: Vâlva Băilor ("dari tambang") adalah pembela dan pelindung tambang dan terowongan; kepergiannya berarti endapan bijih akan habis. Legenda tentangnya berkembang di daerah tambang logam tradisional di Rumania.
statement.en: Vâlva Băilor ("of the mines") is the defender and protector of mines and tunnels, whose departure means the deposit is running out. Legends of her flourish in traditional metal-mining areas of Romania.

claims.quote: Вылва (рум. Vâlva) — в румынской мифологии женский дух, бродящий ночью по вершинам холмов. Вылвы могут быть как добрыми (vâlve albe, белые), так и злыми (vâlve negre, чёрные).

statement.en: The Russian article calls the Вылва a female spirit of Romanian mythology who roams the hilltops at night and may be good (vâlve albe, white) or evil (vâlve negre, black).

claims.quote: Вылва воды (Vâlva Apei) — защитница водных источников и фонтанов.

statement.en: Vâlva Apei is the protector of water sources and fountains.

claims.quote: Вылвы могут принимать разный облик. Часто они выглядят как женщины, иногда просто как тени или чёрные кошки. Вылвы могут защищать село от бури, града, урагана.

short_description.id: Mhachkay adalah makhluk mirip vampir dalam mitologi Turkik dan Tatar: orang berjiwa dua yang bangkit setelah mati dan terbang sebagai burung hantu untuk mengisap darah.
short_description.en: Mhachkay is a vampire-like being of Turkic and Tatar mythology: a person with two souls who rises after death and flies as an owl to suck blood.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Turkik, terutama Tatar, Mhachkay adalah makhluk yang agak mirip vampir. Orang yang lahir dengan dua jantung dan dua jiwa dipercaya sebagai Mhachkay dan diusir dari permukiman. Bila ia mati muda, hanya satu jiwanya pergi; jiwa lainnya menghidupkan jasadnya, yang lalu terbang pada malam hari sebagai burung hantu, menyerang pejalan malam, mengisap darah, dan memakan isi tubuh korban.
long_description.en: In Turkic, especially Tatar, mythology Mhachkay is a somewhat vampire-like being. A person born with two hearts and two souls was thought to be a Mhachkay and was driven from settlements. If such a person died young, only one soul left; the other revived the corpse, which then flew at night as an owl, attacking night travellers, sucking their blood and eating their insides.

long_description.id: Untuk mencegahnya bangkit, jasad Mhachkay dipenggal dan kepalanya dikubur terpisah. Dalam sumber lain, məçkəy dibayangkan sebagai perempuan tua bungkuk pembawa maut yang menyebarkan wabah, seperti Nosferatu.
long_description.en: To stop it rising, a Mhachkay's corpse was beheaded and the head buried apart. In another source the məçkəy is imagined as a hunched old woman spreading death and plague, like Nosferatu.

role.en: Sucks the blood of night travellers.

did_you_know.id: Orang yang lahir dengan dua jantung dan dua jiwa dipercaya sebagai Mhachkay.
did_you_know.en: People born with two hearts and two souls were thought to be Mhachkay.

description.id: Memenggal jasad dan mengubur kepala terpisah mencegahnya bangkit.
description.en: Beheading the corpse and burying the head apart stops it rising.

short_description.id: Joint-eater atau Alp-luachra adalah peri dalam tradisi Kelt yang tanpa terlihat menghabiskan sari makanan korbannya, sehingga korban tetap kurus walau makan banyak.
short_description.en: The joint-eater or Alp-luachra is a fairy of Celtic tradition that invisibly consumes the goodness of its victim's food, so the victim stays thin however much he eats.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Kelt, joint-eater, just-halver, atau Alp-luachra di Irlandia adalah sejenis peri yang duduk tanpa terlihat dan memakan separuh makanan korbannya. Menurut satu versi, ia muncul dalam wujud kadal air ketika seseorang tertidur di tepi mata air atau sungai kecil, lalu merayap masuk lewat mulut dan hidup dari makanan yang ditelan orang itu. Orang yang dihantuinya tidak pernah gemuk, dan orang yang menelan kadal air dipercaya terkena gangguan ini.
long_description.en: In Celtic mythology the joint-eater, just-halver, or in Ireland the Alp-luachra, is a kind of fairy that sits unseen and eats half of its victim's food. In one version it appears as a newt when someone falls asleep beside a spring or stream, crawls in through the mouth and lives off what the person eats. Its victim never grows fat, and people who swallow newts are thought to suffer this way.

long_description.id: Robert Kirk dalam The Secret Commonwealth menulis bahwa orang yang sangat rakus disertai elf rakus bernama Joint-eater atau Just-halver, yang memakan sari dari makanan orang itu sehingga ia tetap kurus seperti elang atau bangau. Andrew Lang dalam pengantar edisi 1893 menjelaskan bahwa orang Highlanders memakai makhluk semacam ini untuk menerangkan nafsu makan yang tidak wajar.
long_description.en: Robert Kirk in The Secret Commonwealth wrote that a great eater is attended by a voracious elf called a Joint-eater or Just-halver, which feeds on the pith or quintessence of his food so that he stays lean like a hawk or heron. In his introduction to the 1893 edition Andrew Lang explains that the Highlanders used such a being to account for a false or morbid appetite.

long_description.id: Kisah "The Alp-Luachra", yang dicatat Hyde dari tuturan penjaga hewan buruan Seamus o h-Airt (James Hart) di barony Frenchpark, menceritakan seorang petani kaya di Connacht yang makin kurus setelah menelan makhluk ini. Ia akhirnya disembuhkan dengan makan banyak daging sapi asin tanpa minum, lalu berbaring dengan mulut terbuka di atas aliran air, hingga anak-anak makhluk itu dan kemudian induknya melompat keluar ke air karena haus.
long_description.en: The tale "The Alp-Luachra", which Hyde recorded from the telling of the Frenchpark game-keeper Seamus o h-Airt (James Hart), tells of a wealthy farmer in Connacht who wasted away after swallowing the creature. He was finally cured by eating much salted beef without drinking and lying with his mouth open over a stream, until the creature's young and then the mother jumped out into the water from thirst.

cultural_context.id: Menurut Andrew Lang, orang Highlanders memakai makhluk ini untuk menjelaskan nafsu makan yang tidak wajar pada orang sakit.

claims.quote: In Celtic mythology, a Joint-eater, Just-halver or Alp-luachra (Ireland) is a type of fairy who sits invisibly and consumes half of their victim's food.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Kelt, Joint-eater, Just-halver, atau Alp-luachra (Irlandia/Ireland) adalah sejenis peri yang duduk tanpa terlihat dan memakan separuh makanan korbannya.
statement.en: In Celtic mythology a Joint-eater, Just-halver or Alp-luachra (Ireland) is a type of fairy that sits invisibly and consumes half of its victim's food.

claims.quote: When a person falls asleep by the side of a spring or stream, the Alp-luachra appears in the form of a newt and crawls down the person's mouth, feeding off the food that they had eaten.

statement.id: Ketika seseorang tertidur di tepi mata air atau sungai kecil, Alp-luachra muncul dalam wujud kadal air (newt) dan merayap masuk lewat mulutnya, lalu memakan makanan yang telah dimakan orang itu.
statement.en: When a person falls asleep beside a spring or stream, the Alp-luachra appears as a newt and crawls down the person's mouth, feeding off the food they have eaten.

claims.quote: A man haunted by a joint-eater will never grow fat, because the pith or quintessence of the food is consumed by the fairy. ... People who consume newts are thought to be plagued in this way.

statement.id: Orang yang dihantui joint-eater tidak akan pernah gemuk karena sari makanan (pith or quintessence) dihabiskan peri itu; orang yang menelan kadal air (newt) dipercaya terkena gangguan ini.
statement.en: A man haunted by a joint-eater never grows fat, because the fairy consumes the pith or quintessence of his food; people who consume newts are thought to be plagued this way.

claims.quote: to rid one's self of an Alp-Luachra, one should eat a large quantity of salt beef, without drinking anything, and then lie by a running stream with their mouth wide open

statement.id: Untuk menyingkirkan Alp-luachra, orang harus makan banyak daging sapi asin tanpa minum, lalu berbaring di tepi aliran air dengan mulut terbuka lebar.
statement.en: To rid oneself of an Alp-luachra one should eat a large quantity of salt beef without drinking, then lie by a running stream with the mouth wide open.

claims.quote: after a long wait, the Alp-Luachra will become thirsty, and will jump into the stream to drink.

statement.id: Setelah lama menunggu, Alp-luachra akan kehausan dan melompat ke sungai untuk minum.
statement.en: After a long wait the Alp-luachra becomes thirsty and jumps into the stream to drink.

claims.quote: They avouch that a Heluo, or Great-eater, hath a voracious Elve to be his attender, called a Joint-eater or Just-halver, feeding on the Pith or Quintessence of what the Man eats; and that therefoir he continues Lean like a Hawke or Heron, notwith standing his devouring Appetite
claims.locator: Secret Commonwealth, section on the subterraneans

statement.id: Menurut Kirk, orang yang rakus (Heluo, Great-eater) disertai elf rakus bernama Joint-eater atau Just-halver yang memakan sari (Pith or Quintessence) dari apa yang dimakan orang itu, sehingga ia tetap kurus seperti elang atau bangau meski nafsu makannya besar.
statement.en: Kirk says a Heluo or Great-eater has a voracious elf attending him, called a Joint-eater or Just-halver, feeding on the Pith or Quintessence of what the man eats, so that he stays lean like a hawk or heron despite his devouring appetite.

claims.quote: By an airy being of this kind the Highlanders explained the false or morbid appetite. A “joint-eater” inhabited the patient; “he feeds two when he eats.”

statement.id: Dengan makhluk halus semacam ini orang Highlanders menjelaskan nafsu makan yang tidak wajar: seekor joint-eater mendiami si sakit, sehingga "ia memberi makan dua ketika ia makan".
statement.en: With an airy being of this kind the Highlanders explained false or morbid appetite: a joint-eater inhabited the patient, so that "he feeds two when he eats".

claims.quote: Any place in Ireland that this herb grows, there be’s an alt-pluachra near it, and you have swallowed an alt-pluachra.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Hyde, seorang pengemis berkata bahwa di mana pun di Irlandia (Ireland) ramuan itu tumbuh, ada alt-pluachra di dekatnya, dan si sakit telah menelan seekor alt-pluachra.
statement.en: In Hyde's tale a beggarman says that anywhere in Ireland this herb grows there is an alt-pluachra near it, and that the sick man has swallowed one.

claims.quote: that’s the reason you’re keeping so thin, for every bit you’re eating the alt-pluachra is getting the good out of it

statement.id: Karena itulah si sakit tetap kurus: setiap suap yang dimakannya, sarinya diambil alt-pluachra.
statement.en: That is why the sick man keeps so thin: of every bit he eats, the alt-pluachra gets the good out of it.

claims.quote: There was once a wealthy farmer in Connacht, and he had plenty of substance and a fine family

statement.id: Kisah itu dibuka dengan seorang petani kaya di Connacht yang berharta banyak dan berkeluarga baik.
statement.en: The tale opens with a wealthy farmer in Connacht who had plenty of substance and a fine family.

claims.quote: “Now the thirst’s coming on them; the salt that was in the beef is working them; now they’ll come out.”

statement.id: Sang pangeran berbisik bahwa rasa haus mulai menyerang mereka karena garam dalam daging sapi, sehingga mereka akan keluar.
statement.en: The prince whispers that thirst is coming on them because of the salt in the beef, so they will come out.

claims.quote: “There’s a dozen of them now,” said the prince; “that’s the clutch; the old mother didn’t come yet.”

statement.id: Sang pangeran menghitung selusin anak alt-pluachra keluar, sementara induknya belum muncul.
statement.en: The prince counts a dozen of them, the clutch, while the old mother has not yet come out.

short_description.id: Boginka adalah roh atau iblis perempuan alam liar dalam mitologi pagan Polandia, sering perwujudan kekuatan alam, yang terkenal menukar bayi manusia.
short_description.en: The boginka is a female spirit or demon of wild nature in Polish pagan mythology, often personifying natural forces, known for swapping human babies.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi pagan Polandia, boginki (tunggal boginka) adalah roh atau iblis perempuan alam liar, seperti hutan, ladang, gunung, atau perairan, dan sering merupakan perwujudan kekuatan alam. Kata ini secara harfiah berarti "dewi kecil" dan dapat diterjemahkan sebagai peri atau nimfa. Mereka dibayangkan sebagai nenek tua buruk rupa atau gadis muda cantik, biasanya telanjang, dan umumnya jahat.
long_description.en: In Polish pagan myth the boginki (singular boginka) are female spirits or demons of the wild, of forest, field, mountain or water, often embodying natural forces. The name literally means "little goddess" and may be rendered as fairy or nymph. They were pictured as hideous crones or lovely young girls, usually naked, and were mostly malevolent.

long_description.id: Istilah boginka kemudian dipakai untuk rusałka, vila, dziwożona, mamuna, dan lainnya. Boginki dapat mencuri bayi manusia dan menggantinya dengan anak pengganti yang disebut odmieniec atau podrzutek. Fungsi utama mereka adalah mengejar perempuan yang baru melahirkan dan perempuan hamil serta menculik dan menukar bayi. Di wilayah Orava dan Spiš mereka digambarkan buruk rupa dengan kepala besar, perut buncit, kaki bengkok, dan payudara besar yang disampirkan ke belakang bahu, dan dapat tampil sebagai kucing, anjing, atau katak.
long_description.en: The word boginka came to cover the rusałka, vila, dziwożona, mamuna and others. Boginki can steal a human baby and leave a substitute called odmieniec or podrzutek. Their chief role is to hound new mothers and pregnant women and to steal and swap babies. In Orava and Spiš they are described as ugly, with big heads, swollen bellies, crooked legs and large breasts thrown back over the shoulder, and they can appear as cats, dogs or frogs.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat Polandia, perempuan yang mati saat melahirkan, bunuh diri, atau membunuh anaknya menjadi boginka. Mereka tinggal di rawa, danau, sungai, hutan, dan gunung, dan dapat dijumpai di tepi air saat mencuci kain dengan pemukul kayu.
long_description.en: Polish folk belief held that women who died in childbirth, took their own lives or killed their children became boginki. They dwelt in marshes, lakes, rivers, forests and mountains and could be met by the water beating cloth with wooden paddles.

short_description.id: Eryr Gwern Abwy, Elang Gwern Abwy, adalah salah satu Hewan Tertua dalam mitologi Wales yang muncul dalam kisah Culhwch ac Olwen dan menuntun para utusan Arthur kepada Salmon dari Llyn Llyw.
short_description.en: The Eagle of Gwern Abwy (Eryr Gwern Abwy) is one of the Oldest Animals of the mythology of Wales who appears in the tale of Culhwch ac Olwen and guides Arthur's envoys to the Salmon of Llyn Llyw.

long_description.id: Eryr Gwern Abwy adalah salah satu Hewan Tertua (Anifeiliaid Hynaf) dalam mitologi Wales dan disebut dalam kisah Culhwch ac Olwen. Dalam Trioedd ia termasuk Tri Hynaif Byd bersama Tylluan Cwm Cowlyd dan Mwyalchen Gelli Gadarn. Lokasi Gwern Abwy sendiri tidak diketahui. Elang adalah burung penting dalam mitologi bangsa Kelt (Celtiaid) dan dikaitkan dengan Matahari.
long_description.en: Eryr Gwern Abwy is one of the Oldest Animals (Anifeiliaid Hynaf) in the mythology of Wales and is mentioned in the tale Culhwch ac Olwen. In the Trioedd he is among the Tri Hynaif Byd alongside Tylluan Cwm Cowlyd and Mwyalchen Gelli Gadarn. The location of Gwern Abwy itself is unknown. The eagle (eryr) is an important bird in the mythology of the Celtiaid and is associated with the Sun.

long_description.id: Dalam terjemahan kisah itu, burung hantu menuntun para utusan ke Elang Gwern Abwy, yang disebut sebagai makhluk paling tua sekaligus paling jauh mengembara. Elang itu bercerita tentang sebuah batu yang dahulu ia patuk bintang-bintangnya dari puncak dan kini tingginya tak sampai sejengkal. Para utusan menanyakan Mabon, putra Modron.
long_description.en: In the translation of the tale, the owl leads the envoys to the Eagle of Gwern Abwy, described as the most ancient creature and the greatest traveller. The eagle speaks of a rock from whose summit he once pecked at the stars, now no more than a span tall. The envoys ask after Mabon the son of Modron.

long_description.id: Elang itu tidak tahu di mana Mabon berada, kecuali sekali ketika ia mencari makan sampai ke Llyn Llyw dan mencengkeram seekor salmon yang menyeretnya ke kedalaman. Ia lalu menuntun para utusan kepada salmon itu, Eog Llyn Llyw, yang diduga tahu lebih banyak.
long_description.en: The eagle does not know where Mabon is, except that once, searching for food as far as Llyn Llyw, he struck a salmon that dragged him into the deep. He then guides the envoys to that salmon, Eog Llyn Llyw, who may know more.

short_description.id: Markut, juga disebut Merküt atau Bürküt, adalah burung legendaris berwujud elang dalam tradisi Altai dan Mongol yang melindungi dan membimbing dukun; di kalangan Yörük di Anatolia ia menjadi sosok untuk menakuti anak nakal.
short_description.en: Markut, also called Merküt or Bürküt, is a legendary eagle-like bird of Altay and Mongol tradition that protects and guides shamans; among the Yörüks of Anatolia it became a figure used to frighten naughty children.

long_description.id: Menurut kamus kedua, Markut adalah elang legendaris dalam mitologi Altai dan Mongol. Ia menjaga para dukun, menuntun jiwa mereka saat melakukan perjalanan ke langit, dan menggendong mereka kembali ke bumi bila tenaga mereka habis. Dalam doa dukun Altai, ia disapa sebagai burung yang sayap kirinya menutupi Bulan, sayap kanannya Matahari, dan sebagai ibu sembilan elang.
long_description.en: According to the second source, Markut is a legendary eagle in Altay and Mongol mythology. It watches over shamans, leads their souls on the journey into the sky and carries them back down to earth on its back once their strength fails. Altai shamans' prayers address it as the bird whose left wing hides the Moon and whose right wing hides the Sun, and as the mother of nine eagles.

long_description.id: Artikel pertama mengutip catatan Radlov tentang ritual kurban dukun di Pegunungan Altai. Markut di sana tidak kasatmata, hanya bisa dilihat orang tertentu, dan dipanggil untuk mengusir roh jahat. Setelah burung itu menjawab panggilan, dukun menirukan suaranya lalu menekuk leher untuk memperlihatkan beratnya memikul burung besar itu.
long_description.en: The first article draws on Radlov's account of shamans' sacrificial rites in the Altay mountains. There Markut is unseen, visible only to certain people, and is called upon to scare off evil spirits. Once the bird answers the call, the shaman imitates its cry and then bends his neck to show how heavy the great bird is to bear.

long_description.id: Pada genderang dukun Teleüt terdapat gambar burung berwujud elang besar bernama Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt, dan dalam pandangan dukun Altay-Sayan burung berwajah cahaya yang menemani Ülgen saat ritual juga disebut Merküt. Artikel pertama juga melihat kedekatan makna antara Markut, Bürküt Ata pada orang Turkmen, dan kepercayaan Yakut bahwa dukun berasal dari keturunan Bürküt.
long_description.en: Teleüt shamans' drums bear the image of a great eagle-like bird called Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt, and in the Altay-Sayan shamans' view the light-faced bird that accompanies Ülgen during rites is likewise called Merküt. The first article also notes a closeness in meaning between Markut, Bürküt Ata of the Turkmens and the Yakut belief that shamans descend from the Bürküt line.

long_description.id: Jauh dari Siberia, di kalangan Yörük semi-nomaden di Anatolia, Merküt menjadi makhluk khayalan yang dikaitkan dengan anak-anak. Di sana ia dikenal sebagai burung legendaris yang dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak nakal, dan menurut kepercayaan lama ia hanya menakuti orang yang namanya disebut.
long_description.en: Far from Siberia, among the semi-nomadic Yörüks of Anatolia, Merküt became an imaginary being connected with children. There it is known as a legendary bird used to scare naughty children, and in the old belief it frightens only those whose names are spoken.

claims.quote: Kötü ruhları korkutmak amacıyla çağırılan Markut adındaki bu kuş ile Türkmenlerdeki Bürküt Ata ve Yakutların, şamanların Bürküt soyundan gelme inançları arasında mitolojik anlamsallık açısından yakınlık bulunmaktadır.

statement.en: The bird Markut, summoned to frighten evil spirits (kötü ruhları), is mythologically close to Bürküt Ata among the Turkmens (Türkmenlerdeki) and to the Yakut (Yakutların) belief that shamans (şamanların) descend from the Bürküt lineage.

statement.en: The Markut mentioned by Radlov is invisible (göze görünmez) and is summoned to frighten evil spirits; only certain people (belli insanlar) can see it.

claims.quote: Şaman, Markut kuşunu bu yolla çağırdıktan sonra cevap verdiği zaman, kuşun sesini taklit eder

statement.en: After the shaman (şaman) summons the Markut bird in this way and it answers, he imitates the bird's voice (kuşun sesini taklit eder).

statement.en: In the worldview of the Altay-Sayan shamans, the light-faced bird (nur yüzlü kuş) accompanying Ülgen during the shamanic rite (kamlık) is also named Merküt.

statement.en: This Merküt bird, far from Siberia (Sibirya), took the form among the semi-nomadic Yörüks of Anatolia (Anadolu) of an imaginary being that protects children (çocukları koruyan).

statement.id: Markut adalah elang legendaris (efsânevî kartal) dalam mitologi Altai (Altay) dan Mongol (Moğol); ia melindungi para dukun (şamanları korur) dan membimbing jiwa mereka dalam perjalanan ke langit (göğe yaptıkları yolculukta).
statement.en: Markut is the legendary eagle (efsânevî kartal) of Altay and Mongol (Moğol) mythology; it protects shamans (şamanları korur) and guides their souls on their journey to the sky (göğe yaptıkları yolculukta).

claims.quote: Güçleri tükenince sırtında yeryüzüne indirir. Anadolu'da yörük boyları arasında da rastlanan bir motiftir.

statement.id: Ketika tenaga mereka habis (güçleri tükenince), ia membawa mereka turun ke bumi di punggungnya; motif ini juga dijumpai di antara suku Yörük di Anatolia (Anadolu'da yörük boyları).
statement.en: When their strength runs out (güçleri tükenince), it carries them down to earth on its back; the motif is also found among the Yörük tribes of Anatolia (Anadolu'da yörük boyları).

claims.quote: Sol kanadı Ay'ı örter/Sağ kanadı Güneş'i/Ey dokuz kartalın anası!

statement.id: Dalam doa dukun Altai, burung ini disapa: sayap kirinya menutupi Bulan (Ay), sayap kanannya Matahari (Güneş), wahai ibu sembilan elang (dokuz kartalın anası).
statement.en: In Altai shamans' prayers the bird is addressed: its left wing covers the Moon (Ay), its right wing the Sun (Güneş), O mother of nine eagles (dokuz kartalın anası).

summary.id: Dalam tradisi dukun Altai dan Mongol, Markut adalah elang pelindung dan pembimbing dukun.
summary.en: In Altay and Mongol shamanic tradition, Markut is an eagle that protects and guides shamans.

summary.id: Di kalangan Yörük, Markut adalah burung yang direka untuk menakuti anak nakal, meski artikel pertama juga menyebutnya makhluk yang melindungi anak.
summary.en: Among the Yörüks, Markut is a bird invented to frighten naughty children, though the first article also calls it a being that protects children.

long_description.id: Kultusnya diketahui setidaknya sejak masa Dinasti Awal. Ia dianggap sebagai istri Khnum yang membentuk tubuh anak dengan roda tembikar. Dalam mitos Osiris ia memberikan napas hidup kepada Horus saat lahir. Sumber pendamping menggambarkannya sebagai katak atau perempuan berkepala katak.
long_description.en: Her cult is known from at least the Early Dynastic Period. She is regarded as wife of Khnum, who shapes children’s bodies on a potter’s wheel. In the Osiris myth she breathes life into Horus at birth. The accompanying source depicts her as a frog or frog-headed woman.

claims.quote: Heqet (Egyptian ḥqt, also ḥqtyt "Heqtit"), sometimes spelled Heket, is an Egyptian goddess of fertility, identified with Hathor, represented in the form of a frog.

statement.id: Heqet adalah dewi kesuburan Mesir yang digambarkan sebagai katak.
statement.en: Heqet is an Egyptian fertility goddess depicted as a frog.

claims.quote:
To the Egyptians, the frog was an ancient symbol of fertility, related to the annual flooding of the Nile. 
Heqet was originally the female counterpart of Khnum, or the wife of Khnum, and eventually she also became the mother of Heru-ur.
It has been proposed that her name is the origin of the name of Hecate, the Greek goddess of witchcraft.

statement.id: Katak berkaitan dengan banjir tahunan Nil dan kesuburan.
statement.en: The frog is linked with the annual Nile flood and fertility.

claims.quote: The beginning of her cult dates to the Early Dynastic Period at least. Her name was part of the names of some high-born Second Dynasty individuals buried at Helwan, such as prince Nisuheqet, and was mentioned on a stela of Wepemnofret and in the Pyramid Texts. Early frog statuettes are often thought to be depictions of her.

statement.id: Kultusnya diketahui setidaknya sejak masa Dinasti Awal.

claims.quote: In the Osiris myth, it was Heqet who breathed life into the new body of Horus at birth, as she was a goddess of the last moments of birth. As the birth of Horus became more intimately associated with the resurrection of Osiris, so Heqet's role became one more closely associated with resurrection.

short_description.id: Bäckahästen, "kuda sungai", adalah kuda air dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, terutama Skåne: kuda putih megah yang memikat orang, terutama anak-anak, menungganginya lalu menenggelamkan mereka.
short_description.en: Bäckahästen, the 'brook horse', is a water horse of Scandinavian, especially Scanian, folklore: a majestic white horse that lures people, above all children, onto its back and drowns them.

long_description.id: Bäckahästen (dari bahasa Swedia bäck, "sungai kecil", dan hästen, "kuda") dalam kepercayaan rakyat Skåne adalah roh sungai atau Näck dalam wujud kuda. Ia dapat dibandingkan dengan kuda air mitologi Kelt seperti each uisge dari Skotlandia, kelpie, dan ceffyl dŵr dari Wales.
long_description.en: Bäckahästen (from Swedish bäck, 'brook', and hästen, 'the horse') is, in Scanian folk belief, the spirit of a brook or the Näck in horse form. It can be compared with the water horses of Celtic mythology such as the Scottish each uisge, the kelpie and the Welsh ceffyl dŵr.

long_description.id: Ia pemangsa licik yang mengintai di sungai dan danau untuk menyeret penunggang dan kuda lain ke air. Wujudnya kuda jantan gagah yang biasanya putih berkilau, kadang kelabu, hitam, atau kebiruan, dengan mulut penuh taring tajam, dan sering muncul saat berkabut. Siapa yang naik ke punggungnya tak bisa turun lagi, dan punggungnya makin panjang semakin banyak anak yang naik.
long_description.en: It is a treacherous predator lurking in brooks, rivers and lakes to drag riders and other horses into the water. It appears as a fine stallion, usually shining white, sometimes dapple-grey, black or bluish, with a mouth full of sharp fangs, and often shows itself in fog. Whoever climbs onto its back cannot get down, and its back grows longer the more children climb on.

long_description.id: Untuk mencegahnya menenggelamkan anak-anak, orang dapat melempar sepotong baja di antara kuda itu dan air, sehingga kekuatannya patah; anak yang menyerukan kata "salib" juga membuatnya melempar mereka dan menghilang. Kuda ini juga bisa dipasangi bajak dan bekerja keras sepanjang hari, karena dijinakkan oleh baja pada tali kekangnya.
long_description.en: To stop it drowning children one can throw a piece of steel between the horse and the water, breaking its power; a child calling out the word 'cross' also makes it throw them off and vanish. It can also be put to the plough and work hard all day, tamed by the steel in its harness.

role.id: Memikat orang naik lalu menceburkan mereka ke air.
role.en: Lures riders on and plunges them into water.

note.en: It is held to be the Näck in horse form.

claims.quote: Bäckahästen (schwedisch, von bäck „Bach“ und hästen „das Pferd“) ist im schonischen Volksglauben der Geist eines Baches oder der Näck in Pferdegestalt. Es kann mit den Wasserpferden aus der keltischen Mythologie wie dem schottischen Each Uisge, dem schottisch-irischen Kelpie oder dem walisischen Ceffyl dŵr verglichen werden.

statement.id: Bäckahästen (Swedia: bäck, "sungai kecil", dan hästen, "kuda") dalam kepercayaan rakyat Skåne adalah roh sungai atau Näck dalam wujud kuda, yang dapat dibandingkan dengan kuda air mitologi Kelt seperti each uisge Skotlandia, kelpie, dan ceffyl dŵr Wales.
statement.en: Bäckahästen (Swedish bäck 'brook' and hästen 'the horse') is in Scanian folk belief a brook spirit or the Näck in horse form, comparable with Celtic water horses such as the Scottish each uisge, the kelpie and the Welsh ceffyl dŵr.

claims.quote: Das Bäckahäst ist ein hinterhältiges Raubtier, das an Bächen, Flüssen und Seen lauert, wo es Reiter und andere Pferde ins Wasser zieht, um sie zu ertränken. Es zeigt sich als stattlicher Hengst, meist weiß schimmernd, aber sein Fell kann auch apfelgrau, schwarz oder blau changieren. Sein Maul ist voller scharfer Fangzähne.

statement.id: Bäckahäst adalah pemangsa licik yang mengintai di sungai dan danau untuk menyeret penunggang dan kuda lain ke air dan menenggelamkannya; ia tampak sebagai kuda jantan gagah yang biasanya putih berkilau, kadang kelabu belang, hitam, atau kebiruan, dengan mulut penuh taring tajam.
statement.en: The bäckahäst is a treacherous predator lurking by brooks, rivers and lakes, dragging riders and other horses into the water to drown them; it appears as a fine stallion, usually shimmering white, sometimes dapple-grey, black or blue, its mouth full of sharp fangs.

claims.quote: Die Anzahl der Kinder spielt dabei keine Rolle, da der Pferderücken immer länger wird, je mehr Kinder sich auf das Untier setzen. Wenn man ein Bäckahäst daran hindern will, Kinder zu ertränken, soll man ein Stück Stahl zwischen das Pferd und das Wasser werfen. ... Eine andere Möglichkeit, dem Untier zu entkommen, besteht darin, dass ein Kind das christliche Wort „Kreuz“ ausruft

statement.id: Jumlah anak tak jadi soal karena punggung kuda makin panjang semakin banyak anak yang naik; untuk mencegahnya menenggelamkan anak, orang melempar sepotong baja di antara kuda dan air, atau seorang anak menyerukan kata Kristen "salib".
statement.en: The number of children does not matter, as the horse's back grows longer the more climb on; to stop it drowning children, throw a piece of steel between horse and water, or a child may cry out the Christian word 'cross'.

claims.quote: Le bäckahäst, bäckahästen ou bækhesten (littéralement « cheval des ruisseaux ») est un cheval fantastique issu du folklore scandinave, très proche du kelpie. Il s'agit d'un majestueux cheval blanc qui apparait près des rivières, en particulier par temps de brouillard. Celui qui monte sur son dos se trouve incapable d'en descendre.

statement.id: Bäckahäst, bäckahästen, atau bækhesten (harfiah "kuda sungai kecil") adalah kuda khayalan cerita rakyat Skandinavia yang sangat mirip kelpie: kuda putih megah yang muncul dekat sungai, terutama saat berkabut, dan siapa yang naik ke punggungnya tak bisa turun.
statement.en: The bäckahäst, bäckahästen or bækhesten ('brook horse') is a fantastic horse of Scandinavian folklore very close to the kelpie: a majestic white horse appearing near rivers, especially in fog, and whoever mounts it cannot get off.

claims.quote: Bækhesten eller Bäckahästen (fra svensk: bäckhästen) er et mytologisk dyr i nordisk folklore og skånsk folketro, svarende til nøkken, blot i hesteform. Hesten er den skandinaviske udgave af den keltiske Kelpie

statement.id: Bækhesten atau Bäckahästen adalah hewan mitos dalam cerita rakyat Nordik dan kepercayaan Skåne, padanan nøkken dalam wujud kuda, dan versi Skandinavia dari kelpie Kelt.
statement.en: Bækhesten or Bäckahästen is a mythical animal of Nordic folklore and Scanian belief, the nøkk in horse form, and the Scandinavian version of the Celtic kelpie.

claims.quote: Im schwedischen Volksglauben wird weiter berichtet, dass das Bäckahäst einem Bauern erlaubte, es vor den Pflug zu spannen ... Der Hengst war durch den Stahl im Pferdegeschirr während der Tagesarbeit gebändigt worden.

statement.id: Menurut kepercayaan Swedia, bäckahäst pernah membiarkan seorang petani memasangnya pada bajak; kuda jantan itu jinak sepanjang hari kerja karena baja pada tali kekangnya.
statement.en: In Swedish belief the bäckahäst let a farmer harness it to the plough; the stallion was tamed through the working day by the steel in its harness.

short_description.id: Drudwyn adalah anjing pemburu dalam mitologi Welsh, salah satu Cŵn Annwn, yang menurut kisah Kilhwch and Olwen mutlak diperlukan untuk memburu babi hutan Twrch Trwyth.
short_description.en: Drudwyn is a hunting hound of Welsh mythology, one of the Cŵn Annwn, who in the tale of Kilhwch and Olwen is indispensable for hunting the boar Twrch Trwyth.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Welsh, Drudwyn tergolong Cŵn Annwn, anjing-anjing Annwn. Ia digambarkan bertelinga merah dan bertubuh putih. Dalam terjemahan Guest ia disebut anak anjing milik Greid putra Eri, sedangkan Wikipedia Jerman menyebutnya anjing muda Greid dan putra Eri.
long_description.en: In Welsh mythology Drudwyn is one of the Cŵn Annwn, the hounds of Annwn. He is described as having red ears and a white body. Guest's translation calls him the whelp of Greid the son of Eri, while the German Wikipedia calls him the young dog of Greid and a son of Eri.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah Kilhwch and Olwen, Drudwyn masuk daftar tugas yang hampir mustahil: babi hutan Twrch Trwyth tidak bisa diburu tanpa dia. Tidak ada tali kekang yang dapat menahannya kecuali tali kekang Cwrs Cant Ewin, dan menurut Kai hanya tali dari janggut Dillus Varvawc yang mampu mengikatnya. Hanya Mabon putra Modron yang dapat berburu bersamanya.
long_description.en: In the tale of Kilhwch and Olwen, Drudwyn is part of the near-impossible tasks: the boar Twrch Trwyth cannot be hunted without him. No leash can hold him except the leash of Cwrs Cant Ewin, and according to Kai only a leash made from the beard of Dillus Varvawc can bind him. Only Mabon the son of Modron can hunt with him.

long_description.id: Setelah Arthur memutuskan untuk mencari Drudwyn, anjing itu ikut dalam perburuan Yskithyrwyn Penbaedd bersama dua anjing Glythmyr Ledewic, walaupun babi hutan itu akhirnya dibunuh oleh Cavall, anjing Arthur sendiri. Dalam perburuan Twrch Trwyth, Eli dan Trachmyr menuntun Drudwyn. Wikipedia Jerman meringkasnya dengan menyebut Drudwyn menangkap Twrch Trwyth untuk Mabon ap Modron sehingga Mabon dapat merebut sisir dan gunting dari babi hutan itu.
long_description.en: After Arthur decided to seek Drudwyn, the hound took part in the hunt of Yskithyrwyn Penbaedd together with the two dogs of Glythmyr Ledewic, though that boar was finally slain by Cavall, Arthur's own dog. In the hunt of Twrch Trwyth, Eli and Trachmyr led Drudwyn. The German Wikipedia summarises this by saying Drudwyn caught Twrch Trwyth for Mabon ap Modron so that Mabon could snatch the comb and scissors from the boar.

short_description.id: Eog Llyn Llyw adalah ikan salmon (eog) dari kisah Culhwch ac Olwen, yang disebut sebagai yang tertua dan terbijak di antara Hewan-Hewan Tertua; ia mengantar utusan Arthur ke penjara Mabon fab Modron.
short_description.en: Eog Llyn Llyw, the Salmon of Llyn Llyw, is a salmon (eog) in the tale Culhwch ac Olwen, called the oldest and wisest of the Oldest Animals; it carries Arthur's envoys to the prison of Mabon fab Modron.

long_description.id: Eog Llyn Llyw muncul dalam kisah Culhwch ac Olwen sebagai salah satu Hewan-Hewan Tertua (Anifeiliaid Hynaf), dan menurut satu ensiklopedia daring ia yang tertua dan terbijak di antara mereka. Salah satu tugas mustahil (anoethau) yang diberikan Ysbaddaden Bencawr kepada Culhwch adalah membebaskan Mabon fab Modron dari penjaranya. Utusan Arthur menanyai hewan-hewan tua satu demi satu, dan Eryr Gwern Abwy (Elang Gwern Abwy) membawa mereka kepada sang salmon.
long_description.en: Eog Llyn Llyw appears in the tale Culhwch ac Olwen as one of the Oldest Animals (Anifeiliaid Hynaf), and according to one online encyclopedia it is the oldest and wisest of them. One of the impossible tasks (anoethau) that Ysbaddaden Bencawr sets Culhwch is to free Mabon fab Modron from his prison. Arthur's envoys question the old animals in turn, and Eryr Gwern Abwy (the Eagle of Gwern Abwy) leads them to the salmon.

long_description.id: Dalam terjemahan Guest, sang elang bercerita bahwa ia pernah mencengkeram salmon itu di Llyn Llyw untuk dimakan, tetapi salmon itu menyeretnya ke dalam air dalam sehingga ia nyaris tidak bisa lolos. Elang itu kemudian menyerangnya bersama seluruh kerabatnya, tetapi salmon itu mengirim utusan untuk berdamai dan meminta sang elang mencabut lima puluh tombak ikan dari punggungnya.
long_description.en: In Guest's translation the eagle relates that it once struck its talons into the salmon at Llyn Llyw for food, but the salmon drew it into the deep so that it barely escaped. The eagle then attacked it with its whole kindred, but the salmon sent messengers to make peace and asked the eagle to take fifty fish spears out of its back.

long_description.id: Sang salmon menjelaskan bahwa setiap pasang ia berenang menyusuri sungai ke hulu hingga dekat tembok Caerloyw (Gloucester), dan di sana ia mendengar ratapan dari penjara. Ia menawarkan untuk membawa para utusan di atas kedua bahunya; mereka sampai ke tembok penjara dan berbicara dengan tahanan yang ternyata Mabon fab Modron. Ketika Arthur dan pasukannya menyerang kastel, Cei dan Bedwyr menyusuri sungai di atas bahu sang salmon, lalu Cei menjebol tembok dan membebaskan Mabon.
long_description.en: The salmon explains that with every tide it goes up the river until it comes near the walls of Caerloyw (Gloucester), and there it hears wailing from the prison. It offers to carry the envoys on its two shoulders; they reach the prison wall and speak with the prisoner, who is Mabon fab Modron. When Arthur and his host attack the castle, Cei and Bedwyr travel along the river on the salmon's shoulders, and Cei breaks through the walls and frees Mabon.

long_description.id: Eog Llyn Llyw dapat digolongkan bersama banyak contoh salmon adikodrati di dunia Celtic, tempat salmon dikaitkan dengan pengetahuan dan kebijaksanaan; pahlawan Irlandia Finn mac Cumaill, misalnya, memperoleh karunia nabi dan orang bijak setelah menyentuh salmon istimewa lalu memasukkan ibu jarinya ke mulut. Letak Llyn Llyw tidak pasti, tetapi karena salmon itu berenang ke hulu menuju Caerloyw, danau itu diduga berada di sekitar bagian hilir Afon Hafren.
long_description.en: Eog Llyn Llyw can be classed with the many examples of supernatural salmon in the Celtic world, where the salmon is associated with knowledge and wisdom; the Irish hero Finn mac Cumaill, for example, gains the gift of a prophet and sage after touching a special salmon and putting his thumb in his mouth. The location of Llyn Llyw is uncertain, but because the salmon swims upriver to Caerloyw, it is thought to lie around the lower part of Afon Hafren.

cultural_context.id: Salmon adikodrati muncul berulang kali di dunia Celtic dan dikaitkan dengan pengetahuan serta kebijaksanaan; Eog Llyn Llyw termasuk golongan ini.
cultural_context.en: Supernatural salmon recur in the Celtic world and are associated with knowledge and wisdom; Eog Llyn Llyw belongs to this group.

statement.id: Eog Llyn Llyw adalah yang tertua (hynaf) dan terbijak (doethaf) di antara Hewan-Hewan Tertua (Anifeiliaid Hynaf) yang disebut dalam kisah (chwedl) Culhwch ac Olwen.

statement.en: One of the Anoethau (impossible tasks, tasgau amhosibl) set on the hero Culhwch by Ysbaddaden Bencawr in the tale is to free (rhyddhau) Mabon fab Modron from his prison (garchar).

statement.id: Sang salmon (Eog) menjelaskan bahwa ia biasa berenang (nofio) menyusuri sungai (afon) setiap malam sampai ke tembok Caerloyw (Gloucester), tempat ia mendengar rintihan mengerikan dari menara kastel.
statement.en: The Salmon (Eog) explains that it used to swim (nofio) along the river (afon) every night until it came to the walls of Caerloyw (Gloucester), where it heard terrible groaning from the castle tower.

claims.quote: Mae'n cynnig cludo Gwrhyr ac Eidoel ar ei ysgwyddau i weld drostynt eu hunain. Llwyddant i siarad â'r carcharor sydd neb llai na Mabon fab Modron.

statement.id: Ia menawarkan untuk membawa (cludo) Gwrhyr dan Eidoel di atas bahunya (ysgwyddau) agar mereka melihat sendiri; mereka berhasil berbicara dengan tahanan (carcharor), yang tak lain adalah Mabon fab Modron.
statement.en: It offers to carry (cludo) Gwrhyr and Eidoel on its shoulders (ysgwyddau) to see for themselves; they manage to speak with the prisoner (carcharor), who is none other than Mabon fab Modron.

claims.quote: aiff Cei a Bedwyr ar hyd yr afon ar ysgwyddau Eog Llyn Llyw. Cyrhaeddent y tŵr ar lan yr afon ac mae Cei yn rhwygo'r muriau ac yn rhyddhau Mabon.

statement.id: Cei dan Bedwyr menyusuri sungai (afon) di atas bahu (ysgwyddau) Eog Llyn Llyw; mereka sampai ke menara di tepi sungai, dan Cei menjebol tembok (muriau) lalu membebaskan (rhyddhau) Mabon.
statement.en: Cei and Bedwyr go along the river (afon) on the shoulders (ysgwyddau) of Eog Llyn Llyw; they reach the tower on the river bank, and Cei tears down the walls (muriau) and frees (rhyddhau) Mabon.

claims.quote: Gellir dosbarthu Eog Llyn Llyw gyda'r sawl enghraifft o eogiaid goruwchnaturiol ym myd y Celtiaid. Cysylltir yr eog â gwybodaeth a doethineb.

statement.id: Eog Llyn Llyw dapat digolongkan bersama banyak contoh salmon adikodrati (eogiaid goruwchnaturiol) di dunia Celtic (byd y Celtiaid); salmon (eog) dikaitkan dengan pengetahuan (gwybodaeth) dan kebijaksanaan (doethineb).
statement.en: Eog Llyn Llyw can be classed with the many examples of supernatural salmon (eogiaid goruwchnaturiol) in the Celtic world (byd y Celtiaid); the salmon (eog) is associated with knowledge (gwybodaeth) and wisdom (doethineb).

claims.quote: Mae'r arwr Gwyddelig Finn mac Cumaill er enghraifft yn cael dawn proffwyd a doethwr ar ôl rhoi ei fawd yn ei geg ar ôl cyffwrdd eog arbennig.

statement.id: Pahlawan Irlandia (arwr Gwyddelig) Finn mac Cumaill, misalnya, mendapat karunia nabi (proffwyd) dan orang bijak setelah memasukkan ibu jarinya ke mulut sesudah menyentuh salmon (eog) istimewa.
statement.en: The Irish hero (arwr Gwyddelig) Finn mac Cumaill, for example, gains the gift of a prophet (proffwyd) and sage after putting his thumb in his mouth having touched a special salmon (eog).

claims.quote: Mae lleoliad Llyn Llyw yn ansicr, ond mae'r ffaith fod yr Eog yn nofio i fyny'r afon i Gaerloyw yn awgrymu ei fod o gwmpas rhan isaf Afon Hafren.

statement.id: Letak (lleoliad) Llyn Llyw tidak pasti (ansicr), tetapi karena salmon (Eog) itu berenang ke hulu menuju Caerloyw (Gaerloyw), diduga tempat itu berada di sekitar bagian hilir Afon Hafren.
statement.en: The location (lleoliad) of Llyn Llyw is uncertain (ansicr), but the fact that the Salmon (Eog) swims upriver to Caerloyw (Gaerloyw) suggests it lies around the lower part of Afon Hafren.

claims.quote: went in search of food as far as Llyn Llyw. And when I came there, I struck my talons into a salmon, thinking he would serve me as food for a long time. But he drew me into the deep, and I was scarcely able to escape from him.

statement.id: Sang elang bercerita bahwa ia mencari makanan sampai ke Llyn Llyw, mencengkeram seekor salmon dengan cakarnya, tetapi salmon itu menyeretnya ke dalam air dalam (the deep) sehingga ia nyaris tidak bisa lolos.
statement.en: The eagle tells how it went in search of food as far as Llyn Llyw and struck its talons into a salmon, but the salmon drew it into the deep and it was scarcely able to escape.

claims.quote: After that I went with my whole kindred to attack him, and to try to destroy him, but he sent messengers, and made peace with me; and came and besought me to take fifty fish spears out of his back.

statement.id: Elang itu lalu menyerang salmon itu bersama seluruh kerabatnya, tetapi salmon itu mengirim utusan, berdamai, dan memohon agar elang mencabut lima puluh (fifty) tombak ikan dari punggungnya.
statement.en: The eagle then went with its whole kindred to attack the salmon, but the salmon sent messengers, made peace, and besought the eagle to take fifty fish spears out of its back.
